<coding_guidelines>
# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to the backlog (GitHub issues labelled `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`)
  as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs (rule 14).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

Synthesize and review a validation contract for a Factory mission. Mission dir: `/home/user/.factory/missions/e194b9e3-6a67-42b9-bfc9-dd4e1ac23b0c` (call it MD). Do not modify the git repository at `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`; read it as needed (`SPEC.md`, `ai/RULES.md`, PRD).

Read all of them fully.

Outputs (write all three, return their paths):
1. `MD/validation-contract.md` — the final contract. Header: title, one paragraph on sources and precedence (planning notes > SPEC v0.2 > PRD v0.6; architecture.md as design reference), the evidence conventions (screenshot, snapshot, console-errors, terminal-output(...), gh-output, app-log, sqlite-query, file, git-log), the Tool vocabulary, and the surface rules from planning note 4 (browser host primary; Tauri smoke set; owner screenshot at integration). Then areas in this order with these headings: `## Area: S — Walking skeleton (milestone s)`, `## Area: M0 — Stream capture and mapping (milestone m0)`, `## Area: M1 — Board in replay and attach (milestone m1)`, `## Area: M2 — Host (milestone m2)`, `## Area: M3 — Intervention (milestone m3)`, `## Area: M4 — Mission branch, gate and fix loop (milestone m4)`, `## Area: M5 — Time, waste, cost (milestone m5)`, `## Area: M5 — Telemetry export (milestone m5)`, `## Cross-Area Flows`, `## Process and integration gates (milestone final)`. Keep each assertion's exact four-part format (`### ID: title`, description, `Tool:`, `Evidence:`).
2. `MD/validation-state.json` — `{"assertions": {"<ID>": {"status": "pending"}, ...}}` for every ID in the final contract, in contract order.
3. `MD/contract-work/index.md` — a compact index for the orchestrator: one line per assertion `ID | title | milestone | tool`, grouped by area, plus a table of counts per prefix before and after your edits, and a "Decisions needed" list.

Editing rules (apply, then record every change in `MD/contract-work/synthesis-log.md`):
- **Deduplicate process checks.** Area drafts each carry per-milestone process assertions (worktree identity, red-test-before-green commit ordering, `make check` exit 0 in the worktree, coverage ≥ 80 %, commit subject/trailer, no history rewrite, must-not-touch scope checks). - Target: a final count roughly 20–25 % below 287, achieved only by the dedup/merge rules above, never by dropping distinct behaviours.

# Planning notes for mission artifacts (orchestrator, 2026-10-22)

Read this before any other mission file. It records what the owner decided after `SPEC.md` v0.2 was
written, and the readiness facts the mission is built on. Where these notes and `SPEC.md` disagree,
these notes win (owner decisions after the spec); `SPEC.md` is amended as-built at the next
integration (RULES rule 8). Where these notes are silent, `SPEC.md` is the authority.

Repository: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory` (GitHub `dctellya/droid-observatory`).
Mission branch: `mission/observatory-v1` (created from `main` at `c8524c2`; pre-mission commit `2266d3e`).
Owner: David Carbajosa Tesoro (`dct`, GitHub `dctellya`).

## Files to read for context (all in the repository)

- `SPEC.md` (v0.2): §2 mission setup, §3 milestones S, M0–M5 with named tests and acceptance
  commands, §4 versions, §5 architecture, §6 tests, §7 CI, §8 deliverables.
- `ai/RULES.md` (binding), `AGENTS.md` (operational summary), `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` v0.6
  (FR ids, lanes, §7 event kinds, §10 metrics, appendix A canonical event).
- `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md` and
  `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md` (measured facts, pasted numbers).
- `config/observatory.example.toml`, `deny.toml`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`,
  `docs/decisions/*.md`.

## Owner decisions after SPEC v0.1 (2026-10-22), all binding

1. **Session file schema.** Droid session files carry no Droid version. The mapping version is
   selected from the Droid version recorded in the **fixture header** (`droid --version`, 0.247.0
   at capture). Token usage, model, tags and child linkage are read from the sibling
   `<session-id>.settings.json` (`tokenUsage`, `childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId`,
   `inclusiveTokenUsage`, `lastCallTokenUsage`, `assistantActiveTimeMs`, `tags`, `model`,
   `reasoningEffort`, `interactionMode`, `autonomyLevel`). Child sessions are sibling files linked by
   `session_start.callingSessionId` / `callingToolUseId`. JSONL `type` values seen: `message`,
   `todo_state`, `agent_turn_outcome`, `compaction_state`, `session_start`; `modelId`,
   `apiProvider`, `reasoningEffort` sit on assistant messages. Decision file at S integration; SPEC
   §3 M0 / §5.2 amended as-built then.
2. **Keyring.** `keyring-core` 1.0.1 + `apple-native-keyring-store` 1.0.2 (feature `keychain`,
   `set_default_store`) instead of `keyring` 4.x (fails `cargo deny`). Keychain items are generic
   passwords with service `droid-observatory/<name>` and account = the login user (`dct`), not the

## Execution model inside the mission

- Workers and validators of milestone `<m>` (`s`, `m0`, `m1`, `m2`, `m3`, `m4`, `m5`) work only in
  the worktree `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/<m>` on branch `wt/<m>`.
  A stable symlink `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current` points at
  the active milestone's worktree; `services.yaml` commands use it.
- The first feature of each milestone after S is an **integration feature** (skill
  `integration-worker`): it merges the previous milestone (`git merge --no-ff wt/<prev>` into
  `mission/observatory-v1`), runs `make check`, pushes, waits for `mission-checks` green, writes the
  shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `docs/decisions/README.md`,
  `reports/usage|readiness|ci`), records the owner's unlocked-display screenshot path, removes the
  old worktree, creates the new worktree and repoints `current`, then returns to the orchestrator
  with the boundary report (the human answers only here, rule 15).
- Final M5 integration and the single PR `mission/observatory-v1` → `main` are done by the
  orchestrator after the M5 validators pass.
- Tests first (rule 1): a red test is committed before the code that makes it green; the scrutiny
  validator checks the red run exists in the worker log.
- Ports: 3141 for the UI dev server (one `trunk serve` at a time); 3142–3149 scratch. Off-limits:
  5000, 7000, 8000, 11434, 18444–18451, anything already listening.
- Off-limits: `main`, ruleset `main-gate`, `rust-toolchain.toml` without a decision, other
  worktrees, `~/.cargo/config.toml`, keychain values (never printed), `~/.factory/sessions/` is
  read-only (fixtures are copies, committed only after `gitleaks detect --no-git` is clean and a

## architecture
# droid-observatory architecture

Authoritative design for the mission `observatory-v1`. Written for implementation workers (Rust,
Leptos, Tauri, CI) who will not read the PRD. Sources, in precedence order: `planning-notes.md`
(owner decisions after the spec, binding), `SPEC.md` v0.2, `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` v0.6,
`docs/decisions/D-*`, the two readiness reports of 2026-10-22, `config/observatory.example.toml`.
Where the sources leave a choice, the choice here is marked `[arch decision]` with its reason.
Paths are relative to the repository root unless absolute. Numbers are pasted from the readiness
reports; none are estimated.

## 1. System overview and invariants

A Factory Mission writes one JSONL per agent session under `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/`.
`observatory-core` turns those lines (and, later, a hosted JSON-RPC stream, local git and GitHub)
into canonical `Event`s on nine lanes, indexes them in SQLite by pointer, computes views and
metrics; `observatory-cli` exercises core headlessly; `observatory-app` (Tauri 2 shell + Leptos
CSR UI) renders the board. Attach (watch + tail) is the primary live mode; replay is attach at
end of file; host is the secondary path and the only one with a control channel (D-008).

Invariants every worker must keep (a violation is a blocking finding):

| # | Invariant | Where enforced |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | `observatory-core` is synchronous: no `tokio`, no `async fn` in its public API. tokio lives only in `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri`. | `cargo machete` + review; `Cargo.toml` of core has no async runtime |
| I2 | The UI holds no logic: card position, filters, scrubbing, tray count, details data, library entries are functions in `core::view`, unit-tested there. The Leptos crate only renders what the shell sends. | SPEC §6 "UI logic" |
| I3 | Raw lines are read-only and never copied into the store. The store keeps `path, byte_offset, byte_len`; the line is re-read on demand. `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written. | `store` DDL has no payload column; `JsonlSource` opens files read-only |
| I4 | Every `Event` carries `mapping_version` and a `SourcePtr`. | type system; test `every_event_carries_the_mapping_version()` |
| I5 | Unknown raw lines become `EventKind::Unknown { raw_type }`, are counted and shown (tray, CLI final line `unknown events: N`, exported counter), never dropped. | `mapping::map_record` is total: it always returns at least one `Event` |
| I6 | Thresholds and intervals come only from `Config` (`config/observatory.example.toml` is the contract); no literal in code. | `clippy.toml`; review |
| I7 | Secrets come only from the keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>`, account = login user) or, for the GitHub token only, `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Never in config, store, logs, telemetry, test fixtures. The `tracing` layer redacts (§12). | `secrets` module is the only reader |
| I8 | The one outward write is the merge (FR-G5), human-confirmed, named PR and target, logged as a lane-7 event. The app never merges on its own; `policy-merged` is observed, not performed. | `control::merge` is the only caller of `Forge::merge` |
| I9 | Core modules that the UI compiles to wasm (`model`, `mapping`, `view`, `metrics`, `config`) have no platform dependency; platform modules sit behind Cargo features (§2). | `trunk build` of the UI crate |

`EventKind` (`model/kind.rs`): one unit variant per PRD §7 name in CamelCase (`intent.created` →
`IntentCreated`, `qa.scenario.passed` → `QaScenarioPassed`, `gate_command.run` → `GateCommandRun`,
`pr.merged_by_human` → `PrMergedByHuman`, 70 variants over lanes 1–8) plus
`Unknown { raw_type: String }`. Methods: `prd_name(&self) -> Cow<str>` returns the dotted PRD name
(`"finding.blocking"`, `"unknown.event"`); `lane(&self) -> Option<Lane>` returns the PRD lane for
known kinds and `None` for `Unknown` (the session role decides). Serde `[arch decision]`: default
externally tagged with `rename_all = "snake_case"` (`"finding_blocking"`,
`{"unknown":{"raw_type":"todo_state"}}`); derive guarantees the round trip, `prd_name()` is for
display, CLI and the store `kind` column.

`MappingVersion` (`mapping/version.rs`): `enum MappingVersion { V1 }`, serde `"v1"`,
`MappingVersion::LATEST`, `fn for_droid_version(v: &str) -> (MappingVersion, Option<Warning>)` (§5).

Serde rules: all enums `snake_case`; ids `#[serde(transparent)]`; `Timestamp` RFC 3339 with
milliseconds, UTC (`2026-10-22T14:54:47.240Z`); `duration` as `duration_ms: u64`; unknown JSON
fields are rejected on `Event` (`deny_unknown_fields`) so a golden file drift fails loudly.
Test `event_round_trips_through_serde()` covers an event per `SourcePtr` variant and `Unknown`.

## 4. Ingest (`core::ingest`)

### 4.1 Source trait and RawRecord

```rust
pub struct RawRecord { pub ptr: SourcePtr, pub session_id: SessionId, pub bytes: Vec<u8> /* one line, no newline */ }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SourceKind { Jsonl, Rpc, Git, GitHub }

pub trait Source {
    fn kind(&self) -> SourceKind;
    /// Pull the next records. Returns an empty Vec when nothing new is available right now.
    /// Never blocks longer than one poll interval; never returns an error for "no data".
    fn next_batch(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<RawRecord>, IngestError>;
    /// True when every known file has been read to its current end (replay = attach that reached EOF, D-008).
    fn at_eof(&self) -> bool;
}
```

`[arch decision]` `next_batch` + `at_eof` replace SPEC §5.4's `poll`: the name says it pulls, and
`at_eof` is what makes replay and attach one code path (the CLI stops at `at_eof()`, the watcher keeps
calling). `IngestError` (thiserror): `Io { path, source }`, `FileMoved { path }`, `TooLarge { path, mb }`.

### 4.2 JsonlSource (S; sidecar and children M0)

```rust
pub struct JsonlSource { /* files: Vec<TailState { path, session_id, offset: u64, partial: Vec<u8> }>, cfg: IngestConfig */ }
impl JsonlSource {
    pub fn open(root: &Path, cfg: &IngestConfig) -> Result<Self, IngestError>;   // root = the orchestrator .jsonl
    pub fn add_file(&mut self, path: &Path) -> Result<SessionId, IngestError>;   // child or newly discovered file
    pub fn read_at(path: &Path, byte_offset: u64, byte_len: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>, IngestError>; // used by inspect/Details
}
```

Reading rules: open read-only; read from `offset` in chunks of `tail_chunk_kb`; split on `\n`; an
incomplete trailing fragment stays in `partial` until the newline arrives (a writer may be mid-line);
`byte_offset` is the offset of the first byte of the line, `byte_len` excludes the newline; a line
that is not valid JSON is still a `RawRecord` (mapping yields `Unknown { raw_type: "<unparseable>" }`).
Files over `max_session_file_mb` are indexed and a `TooLarge` warning is surfaced once.

Sidecar `<session-id>.settings.json` (`ingest::sidecar`, fields fixed by planning note 1 and verified on
disk 2026-10-22):

`systemPrompt` value is never logged or stored.

as `session_start` (`id`, `callingSessionId`, `callingToolUseId`, `cwd`, `version`); a file whose
`callingSessionId` equals a known session id is a child and is added with `parent_id`. The root is

### 4.3 Watcher (M1, feature `watch`)

```rust
pub struct SessionWatcher { /* notify::RecommendedWatcher + poll fallback */ }
impl SessionWatcher {
    pub fn start(cfg: &IngestConfig) -> Result<Self, IngestError>;  // scans cfg.factory_sessions_dir recursively
    pub fn next_discovered(&mut self) -> Vec<DiscoveredSession>;    // new *.jsonl since last call (notify or poll)
}
pub struct DiscoveredSession { pub path: PathBuf, pub session_id: SessionId, pub parent: Option<SessionId>,
                               pub name: String /* first tag, else session id (FR-L1) */ }
```

Design: `notify` 8.2.0 (FSEvents) for create/modify; a poll every `jsonl_poll_ms` (500) re-stats every
watched file and lists the directory, because FSEvents coalesces and a file created before start would be
missed (PRD §14). Startup scan attaches files modified in the last 24 h as growing [arch decision: a
bound so a directory with hundreds of old sessions does not open them all; older files stay in the
library and open on demand]. At most `max_watched_sessions` (64) files are tailed, newest first; the
UI shows "N sessions not watched". Growth is read by `JsonlSource::next_batch` in one `tail_chunk_kb`
step per poll. Everything runs on one `std::thread` owned by the shell (`backend.rs`), which batches
events toward the UI every `event_batch_ms` (100).

### 4.4 Capture header for live attach

`captures` row per attached directory: `id`, `source_dir`, `droid_version`, `started_at`. No file is
written next to Droid's files.

### 4.5 RpcSource (M2, feature `rpc`)

The shell spawns `droid exec --mission --input-format stream-jsonrpc --output-format stream-jsonrpc
<flags from the launch screen> -f <mission file>` with `tokio::process` (stdin piped, stdout piped,
stderr to a log). Every stdout line is appended verbatim to the spool
`~/.droid-observatory/hosted/<launch-id>.jsonl` `[arch decision]`: a hosted stream exists nowhere else,
`inspect`/Details need a raw line, and the spool is the raw source for `SourcePtr::Rpc` (it is not a
copy of a Droid file). `RpcSource` is a `JsonlSource` over the spool (same tail code, I3 holds).
Control writes go to stdin as JSON-RPC 2.0 requests:

```rust
pub enum HostControl { Pause, Resume, Message { text: String }, Answer { question_id: String, text: String },
                       Approve { request_id: String }, Deny { request_id: String } }
pub struct RpcRequest { jsonrpc: "2.0", id: u64, method: String, params: serde_json::Value }
pub fn encode(c: &HostControl, id: u64) -> RpcRequest;   // method names are confirmed in M2 from `droid exec --help`
                                                         // and the first hosted capture; recorded in the M2 decision file
```

An acknowledgement is the JSON-RPC response with the same `id`; `pause_request_is_written_as_jsonrpc_and_acknowledged()`
asserts it. The child is in its own process group and is killed on window close
(`child_process_is_reaped_on_window_close()`); the readiness report shows why: killing the parent alone
orphans children (`trunk serve` and the app binary reparented to PID 1 in the Tauri run).

### 4.6 GitSource, GitHubSource and the Forge trait (M4)

```rust
pub trait Forge {
    fn pr(&self, branch: &str, target: &str) -> Result<Option<Pr>, ForgeError>;
    fn checks(&self, pr: &Pr) -> Result<Vec<Check>, ForgeError>;      // Actions runs + commit statuses, never check-runs
    fn policy(&self, target: &str) -> Result<MergePolicy, ForgeError>; // rulesets + branch protection
    fn reviews(&self, pr: &Pr) -> Result<Vec<Review>, ForgeError>;
    fn attestations(&self, pr: &Pr) -> Result<Vec<Attestation>, ForgeError>;
    fn merge(&self, pr: &Pr, method: MergeMethod) -> Result<Merged, ForgeError>;
}
pub struct Pr { pub number: u64, pub head_sha: String, pub head: String, pub base: String, pub url: String,
                pub state: PrState /* Open, Merged { by: MergedBy::Human | Policy, at }, Closed */ }
pub struct Check { pub name: String, pub source: CheckSource /* ActionsRun { run_id } | CommitStatus { context } */,
                   pub conclusion: CheckConclusion /* Queued, Running, Passed, Failed, RequiredMissing */, pub url: String }
pub struct MergePolicy { pub requires_human: bool, pub allowed_methods: Vec<MergeMethod>,
                         pub decided_by: RuleAttribution /* Ruleset { id, name } | BranchProtection | ConfigOverride(String) | NoRule */ }
pub enum ForgeError { Forbidden { pr: u64, target: String, missing_permission: &'static str /* "pull_requests:write" */ },
                      RateLimited { reset_at }, Http { status, url }, Other(String) }
```

`GitHubSource` uses the token from `secrets::github_token()` (§12), base `https://api.github.com`,
endpoints: `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls?head={o}:{branch}&base={target}&state=all`,
`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs?head_sha=`, `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`,
`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rules/branches/{target}` and `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets`,
`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/branches/{target}/protection` (404 → no protection),
`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews`, `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/attestations/{subject-digest}` (best effort),
`PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/merge`. The check-runs API is never called (planning note 6). Poll every
`[github].poll_interval_s` (30). HTTP client: `ureq` 3 (blocking, rustls) `[arch decision]`: core has
no tokio (I1); version verified on the day with `make deny`. `GitSource` runs `git` via
`std::process::Command` in the repository: `for-each-ref refs/heads/mission/*`, `worktree list --porcelain`,
`log --first-parent --merges mission/<name>` for integration commits → `IntegrationMerged`; fast-check
runs come from `GET /actions/runs?branch=mission/<name>` → `GateCommandRun/Passed/Failed` attributed to
the milestone whose `wt/<m>` merge commit is the run's head.

Target branch comes from `[github].target_branch` (default `"main"`, §11); the mission branch from
`[mission].branch_pattern`. Merge policy: `[github].merge_policy = "auto"` reads GitHub (`requires_human`
= ruleset/protection requires a PR and no auto-merge is enabled); `"human"` forces the button;
`"policy"` never shows it (`decided_by = ConfigOverride`). Gate badge state machine (`view::gate`):
`Pending` (no PR) → `ChecksRunning` → `ReviewRequested` | `HumanRequired` | `RulesetBlocked` | `CiRed` →
`CiGreen` → `PolicyMerged` | `MergedByHuman`. `PolicyMerged` is set when the poll sees `state = Merged`
with no app merge action in `human_actions` for that PR (`policy_merged_detected_without_human_action()`).

Merge button flow (planning note 7): visible only when `requires_human && all required checks Passed`
(`merge_button_shows_only_when_policy_is_human_and_checks_are_green()`); click → confirmation dialog
naming `PR #n` and `target`; confirm → `control::merge` writes the lane-7 `PrMergedByHuman` intent row
with `state = requested`, calls `Forge::merge`; on `ForgeError::Forbidden` the UI shows exactly
`Merge of PR #<n> into <target> refused: token lacks <missing_permission>. Merge in GitHub; the badge
updates from the next poll.`; no retry, the row becomes `state = refused`, the button stays visible, the
poll continues at the normal interval (no storm). The owner merges; the next poll yields `PolicyMerged`
or `MergedByHuman` depending on the merger login equalling the token owner.


Lane-7 mapping (`each_control_emits_one_lane7_event_with_actor_human()`): every action produces exactly
one event with `lane = Human`, `role = Human`, `source = App { action_id }`. `[arch decision]` lane 7 has
exactly the five PRD kinds and no new kind is invented; the control name is kept in `human_actions.kind`,
which the pointer references:

| Control | `EventKind` | `human_actions.kind` / `state` |
|---|---|---|
| Pause, Resume, Message, MarkComplete, MarkSkipped | `ApprovalGiven` | `pause`, `resume`, `message`, `mark_complete`, `mark_skipped` / `sent` |
| Answer | `QuestionAnswered` | `answer` / `sent`; `payload_ptr` = the `QuestionAsked` event id |
| Approve, Deny | `ApprovalGiven` | `approve` / `granted`, `deny` / `denied`; `payload_ptr` = the `PermissionRequested` event id |
| Merge (M4) | `PrMergedByHuman` | `merge` / `requested` → `merged` or `refused` |

Free text is never stored (only its length); it is relayed to the host over `HostControl` (M2). For an
attached mission there is no control channel (D-008): the UI shows the text as "copy to the terminal
running the mission" and still records the lane-7 event. `MarkSkipped` is relayed as an instruction to

| `last_kind` | Prompt (anchor in `stalled-mission.md`) |
|---|---|
| `QuestionAsked`, `PermissionRequested` | "Waiting on human: answer it" (#waiting-on-human) |
| `SubagentSpawned` with no child growth | "Worker silent: check the child file, retry or skip" (#worker-silent) |
| `HookBlocked` repeated | "Agent hits the write guard: forward-only instruction" (#hook-blocked) |
| `IntegrationConflict` | "Two worktrees touched one file" (#integration-conflict) |
| anything else | "Long tool call: wait one more threshold, then pause and inspect" (#long-tool-call) |

## 9. Metrics (`core::metrics`, M5)

Time states (PRD §10.1): `enum TimeState { Active, WaitingHuman(Question|Permission|Merge), WaitingValidation,
RetryFailure, IdleQueued, IdleUnscheduled }`. `pub fn partition(events_of_feature: &[Event], end: Timestamp)
-> Vec<Interval { from, to, state }>`, contiguous and non-overlapping
(`time_states_partition_every_instant_exactly_once()`). Active intervals `[arch decision]`: each event
with `duration` contributes `[at, at + duration]`; `duration` is set by the mapper as `tool_result.at -
tool_use.at` for tool calls and `assistant.at - previous_line.at` (same session) for model generation.
`ToolError`/`HookBlocked` intervals are `RetryFailure`; an open `QuestionAsked`/`PermissionRequested`/
green-but-unmerged gate with no active interval is `WaitingHuman`; `TaskDone` without a validator start is
`WaitingValidation`; a defined feature blocked by another's active interval is `IdleQueued`, else
`IdleUnscheduled`. The oracle (below) validates these rules.

Rework windows (`metrics::rework`): open/close pairs from PRD §10.2 (`FindingBlocking→ReworkResolved`,
`QaScenarioFailed→QaScenarioPassed` same scenario, `IntegrationConflict→IntegrationConflictResolved`,
`CheckFailed→CheckPassed` same check); overlapping windows on one feature merge; unresolved at mission end
reported with `closed_by = None`. Causes: `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate`.
Overhead (`metrics::overhead`): orchestrator intervals before the first `FeatureDefined`, replanning not
attributable, and compaction recovery; reported as its own line; `[metrics].overhead_apportionment =
"equal"` splits it and labels the output `apportioned`. Derived (`metrics::derived`): cycle (feature,
milestone, mission, per lane), waste by the 8 SPEC §5.6 causes, bottleneck (lane/role with highest
waiting + queued; lane with highest WIP/throughput), fix loops (count of `fix` cycles).

Cost (`metrics::cost`): tokens from `UsageReported` (sidecar `tokenUsage`); credits primary when
`factoryCredits` is present; otherwise `Σ tokens × per_m / 1e6` from `config/prices/<date>.toml`
(`[metrics].price_table`); every `Cost` carries `price_table: String` (the `effective` date)
(`cost_names_the_price_table_date()`). Budget meter: `[metrics].budget` or the launch `budget_usd`.
Model comparison (FR-M7): per role, per model, `cost_per_completed_feature` and
`first_pass_active_s_per_completed_feature`.

Oracle (`tests/oracle.rs`, `reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv`, owner-produced before M5).
Column contract `[arch decision]` (fixed now so the owner can produce it):

```text
scope,id,name,cycle_s,first_pass_active_s,rework_s,waste_waiting_human_question_s,waste_waiting_human_permission_s,
waste_waiting_merge_s,waste_waiting_validation_s,waste_rework_s,waste_retry_failure_s,waste_idle_queued_s,
waste_idle_unscheduled_s,rework_windows,tokens_input,tokens_output,tokens_cache_read,tokens_cache_write,cost_usd,price_table
```

`scope ∈ {feature, milestone}`; durations integer seconds; tolerance 1 s, 1 token, 0.01 USD
(`metrics_match_reference_spreadsheet_within_tolerance()`). `observatory-cli metrics <root.jsonl> --csv`
prints exactly these columns; `--json` prints `MetricsReport`. Export (`metrics::export`): same rows to
CSV (RFC 4180) or JSON at the chosen path.

content: [ {type: text|thinking|tool_use|tool_result, ...} ], modelId?, apiProvider?, reasoningEffort?}}`.
`tool_use` parts: `{id, name, input}`; `tool_result`: `{tool_use_id, content, is_error?}`. Tool names seen:

v1 rules (the frozen table lives in `mapping/v1/kinds.rs` and is reproduced in the M0 decision file):

| Raw shape | EventKind | Lane / role |
|---|---|---|
| `session_start` with no `callingSessionId` | `IntentCreated` (first) | 1, Orchestrator |
| `session_start` with `callingSessionId` | `SubagentSpawned` | 3, child's role |
| user `message`, text, root session, first | `IntentCreated`; later ones `IntentAmended` | 1, Human |
| assistant `tool_use` name `Task` | `TaskAssigned` (+ `FeatureDefined` when the input names a new feature) | 2 |
| assistant `tool_use` name `ProposeMission` | `PlanCreated`; `MilestoneDefined` per milestone in the input | 2 |
| assistant `tool_use` name `AskUser` | `QuestionAsked` | 1 |
| user `tool_result` for an `AskUser` | `IntentAnswered` | 1, Human |
| assistant `tool_use` Execute/Script with `git commit` in the command | `CommitCreated` | 3 |
| assistant `tool_use` Execute/Script with `cargo test`/`make test`/`make check` | `TestsRun`; result `is_error` → `GateCommandFailed` else `GateCommandPassed` when the command is `make check` | 3 / 6 |
| assistant `tool_use` Edit/Create/ApplyPatch | `FileTouched` | 3 |
| `tool_result` with `is_error: true` | `ToolError` (`HookBlocked` when the content names `guard-git.sh`) | 3 |
| assistant message whose `modelId` differs from the previous assistant message of the session | `ModelChanged` | 3 |
| `compaction_state` | `ContextCompacted` | 2 |
| `agent_turn_outcome` in a child session | `TaskDone` (`resultKind`), then `SubagentFinished` at EOF | 3 |
| `todo_state` | `PlanRevised` when todos changed | 2 |
| validator text containing a `## Blocking`/`## Non-blocking` findings block (format fixed in M0 from the capture) | `FindingBlocking` / `FindingNonBlocking` / `ScrutinyPassed`; user-testing `QaScenarioPassed/Failed/Evidence` | 4 / 5 |

Fail if any session lacks a `usage_reported` event or if any of the four token numbers differ from the sidecar.
Tool: shell
Evidence: terminal-output(jq tokenUsage per sidecar), terminal-output(jq usage_reported per session), sqlite-query(SELECT id, tag, model FROM sessions)

### VAL-MAP-015: Store schema has the pointer index and no payload column
Open the store the CLI wrote (`[store].path`, default `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite`, or the path passed through `OBSERVATORY_CONFIG`) with `sqlite3 <db> '.schema'`. It contains the tables `schema_version`, `captures`, `mapping_versions`, `missions`, `sessions`, `milestones`, `features`, `events`, `usage`, `rework_windows`, `prs`, `checks`, `reviews`, `attestations`, `human_actions`, `prices`; `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX events_ptr ON events(path, byte_offset, sub) WHERE path IS NOT NULL`; indexes `events_mission_at` and `events_feature`. `sqlite3 <db> "SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info('events')"` returns exactly the 23 columns `id, mission_id, session_id, milestone_id, feature_id, lane, kind, raw_type, mapping_version, role, model, at, duration_ms, source, path, byte_offset, byte_len, sub, repo, sha, url, action_id` plus none named `text`, `payload`, `raw`, `line` or `content`. `PRAGMA journal_mode` returns `wal`; `SELECT max(version) FROM schema_version` returns 1 or higher. Fail on a missing table, a missing or non-unique pointer index, or any extra payload column.
Tool: sqlite3
Evidence: sqlite-query(.schema), sqlite-query(pragma_table_info('events')), sqlite-query(PRAGMA journal_mode)

### VAL-MAP-016: Raw line text, tool output and `systemPrompt` are never stored
After `observatory-cli replay <m0>.jsonl` has indexed the capture into the store: pick a distinctive substring of at least 40 characters from a `tool_result` content in `<m0>.jsonl` and the first 40 characters of `systemPrompt` from `<m0>.settings.json`; `strings <db> <db>-wal | grep -c -F '<substring>'` returns `0` for both. `sqlite3 <db> "SELECT count(*) FROM events WHERE path IS NULL"` returns `0` for this jsonl-only capture (every row is a pointer). Fail if any substring is found in the database or WAL file.
Tool: sqlite3
Evidence: terminal-output(strings | grep -c for both substrings), sqlite-query(count of events with NULL path)

### VAL-MAP-017: Store records the mapping version and the capture header
`sqlite3 <db> "SELECT version, droid_version_range FROM mapping_versions"` returns one row `v1|0.247.*` (or the equivalent range string frozen in the decision file) with a non-empty `frozen_at`. `sqlite3 <db> "SELECT droid_version, header_path FROM captures"` returns a row with `droid_version = 0.247.0` and `header_path` ending in `2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.capture.json`. `sqlite3 <db> "SELECT count(*) FROM events WHERE mapping_version <> 'v1'"` returns `0`. Fail on a missing row, a different version string, or events referencing another mapping version.
Tool: sqlite3
Evidence: sqlite-query(mapping_versions), sqlite-query(captures), sqlite-query(events mapping_version count)

### VAL-MAP-018: One `sessions` row per JSONL file with parent linkage and role
`sqlite3 <db> "SELECT id, parent_id, role, path FROM sessions ORDER BY id"` returns exactly one row per `.jsonl` in the capture (root + count of `.children/*.jsonl`); the root row has `parent_id` NULL and `role = orchestrator`; every child row has `parent_id` equal to its `callingSessionId` and a `role` equal to the header's role for that id; each `path` is the fixture file the row was read from. `SELECT count(*) FROM sessions WHERE role = 'unresolved'` returns `0`. Fail on a count mismatch, a NULL child `parent_id`, or a role differing from the header.
Tool: sqlite3
Evidence: sqlite-query(sessions rows), terminal-output(ls fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.children/*.jsonl | wc -l)

### VAL-MAP-019: Store pointer reads back the exact raw line
`cargo test -p observatory-core --test store store_pointer_reads_back_the_exact_raw_line` exits 0 and prints `... ok`. The test inserts events mapped from the M0 fixture, reads `pointer(id)` back and asserts `JsonlSource::read_at(path, byte_offset, byte_len)` returns bytes equal to the original line without its trailing newline (architecture §4.2: `byte_len` excludes the newline). Fail if the test is absent, ignored or red.
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: terminal-output(cargo test filtered run)

### VAL-MAP-020: `inspect <event-id>` prints the raw line byte-identically
Choose three event ids from `<m0>.events.json` (`jq -r '.[0].id, .[100].id, .[-1].id'`), one of them from a child session. For each, read `path`, `byte_offset`, `byte_len` from the same element, then compare `cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- inspect <event-id> > /tmp/inspect.out` with `dd if=<repo>/<path> bs=1 skip=<byte_offset> count=<byte_len> 2>/dev/null > /tmp/slice.out` (or `sed -n '<line>p'` with the trailing newline stripped): `cmp /tmp/inspect.out /tmp/slice.out` exits 0, allowing at most one trailing `\n` added by the CLI (check with `wc -c`: the difference is 0 or 1 byte, and `cmp -n <byte_len>` exits 0). Exit code of `inspect` is 0. Fail if any byte within `byte_len` differs or if `inspect` exits non-zero for a valid id.
Tool: cli
Evidence: terminal-output(cmp exit codes for three ids), terminal-output(wc -c of both files)

### VAL-MAP-021: `inspect` on a moved source file names the pointer instead of panicking
Replay a `/tmp` copy of the fixture (as in VAL-MAP-006, header unchanged) into a scratch store, then rename the copied root `.jsonl` and run `cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- inspect <event-id of that session>`. The process does not panic (no `panicked at` in stderr); stderr contains the pointer's `path`, `byte_offset` and `byte_len` (architecture §6: "if the file is gone the error names the pointer (`FileMoved`)"); the exit code is non-zero, consistent with the S CLI convention `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file()`. Fail on a panic, an exit code of 0, or an error message without the pointer fields.
Tool: cli
Evidence: terminal-output(inspect stderr and exit code after the rename)

### VAL-MAP-022: CLI exit codes and last-line contract are covered by the CLI tests
`cargo test -p observatory-cli` exits 0 with `0 failed`, and its output lists `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file ... ok` plus the M0 `inspect` test(s) from `crates/observatory-cli/tests/cli.rs` (architecture §14: exit codes, exact `unknown events: N` last line, `inspect` bytes equal the file slice). Directly: `cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/does-not-exist.jsonl; echo $?` prints a non-zero code and an error naming the path; `cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay <m0>.jsonl >/dev/null; echo $?` prints `0`. Fail if the test suite is red, if the missing-file replay exits 0, or if the valid replay exits non-zero.
Tool: cli
Evidence: terminal-output(cargo test -p observatory-cli result line), terminal-output(two replay exit codes)

### VAL-MAP-023: Mapping stays total: an unrecognised line is counted, not dropped
Append one line that is not valid JSON (for example `not json`) and one JSON line with an unseen `type` (`{"type":"future_kind"}`) to a `/tmp` copy of the root fixture (header and children copied unchanged), then `cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay /tmp/<copy>.jsonl`. The last line is `unknown events: 2`, the event listing shows `unknown.event` with `raw_type` `<unparseable>` for the first and `future_kind` for the second, and the exit code is 0 (invariant I5 and architecture §4.2; rule 18). Fail if either line is dropped, the count differs, or the CLI exits non-zero.
Tool: cli
Evidence: terminal-output(replay of the appended copy: the two unknown lines and the last line)

### VAL-MAP-024: Decision file `D-0NN-mapping-v1.md` freezes the mapping and answers the PRD §11.1 open items
A file `docs/decisions/D-0NN-mapping-v1.md` exists with NN the next free number after D-010 and contains: `**Date:**` and `**Status:**` lines, context, decision, alternatives, consequences (rule 13); the frozen v1 rule table (raw shape → `EventKind` → lane/role, matching `crates/observatory-core/src/mapping/v1/kinds.rs`); the Droid version range the module covers (`0.247.x`); the "defined, not observed" list of PRD §7 kinds (VAL-MAP-011); and one finding each for where `--tag` is recorded (sidecar `tags`), how child sessions link (`session_start.callingSessionId` / `callingToolUseId`), how roles are identified (the parent `Task` `tool_use` `input.subagent_type` strings, exact values), and which `Task`/`ProposeMission` input fields give feature and milestone ids. `make check-decisions-index` exits 0 (index regenerated). Fail if the file, any of the five findings, or the "defined, not observed" list is missing, or if the index is stale.
Tool: shell
Evidence: file(docs/decisions/D-0NN-mapping-v1.md), terminal-output(make check-decisions-index exit code), file(docs/decisions/README.md)

### VAL-MAP-025: Decision files due at S integration exist on the mission branch
On `mission/observatory-v1` after the S → M0 integration feature, `docs/decisions/` contains one file each (D-011 onward, slug of the worker's choosing) recording: the session file schema (Droid version from the fixture header, usage/model/tags/child links from the sibling `.settings.json`; planning note 1), keyring variant B (`keyring-core` 1.0.1 + `apple-native-keyring-store` 1.0.2; note 2), the read-only fine-grained PAT with check results from Actions runs and commit statuses (note 6), backlog = `BACKLOG.md` only with the SPEC §8 hybrid backlog withdrawn (note 9), the coverage component and 80 % threshold (B-005), and `cargo-machete` (B-014). Each has `**Date:**` and `**Status:**`. `SPEC.md` §3 M0 and §5.2 read "selected by the Droid version in the fixture header" (amended as-built, SPEC §10 row added). Fail if any of the six decisions or the SPEC amendment is absent.
Tool: git
Evidence: terminal-output(git -C <mission branch checkout> ls-files docs/decisions), file(docs/decisions/README.md), terminal-output(grep -n "fixture header" SPEC.md)

### VAL-MAP-026: Coverage gate passes at 80 % lines on `observatory-core`
Run alone (planning note 5: no concurrent cargo or trunk job) in `<repo>`: `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --all-features --fail-under-lines 80 --summary-only` exits 0 and the `TOTAL` line reports a lines percentage of at least 80.00 (paste the number, rule 7). SPEC §6: enforced from M0. Confirm at integration that `.github/workflows/mission-branch.yml` sets `COVERAGE_MIN: "80"` (architecture §15: the M0 integration sets it). Fail on a non-zero exit or a percentage under 80.
Tool: shell
Evidence: terminal-output(cargo llvm-cov summary TOTAL line and exit code), file(.github/workflows/mission-branch.yml)

### VAL-MAP-027: M0 touches nothing beyond its scope (no UI, no git/GitHub adapters, no metrics)
In `<repo>`: the directories `crates/observatory-core/src/view`, `crates/observatory-core/src/metrics`, `crates/observatory-core/src/control` and the files `crates/observatory-core/src/ingest/{watch,rpc,git,github,forge}.rs` do not exist; `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 | jq '.packages[] | select(.name=="observatory-core") | .dependencies[].name'` lists neither `ureq`, `notify`, nor `tokio`; `git diff --name-only $(git merge-base wt/m0 mission/observatory-v1) wt/m0 -- apps/observatory-app/ui/src` lists no new component directories (`board/`, `details/`, `agents/`, `lane9/`, `launch/` absent), so the window still shows the nine empty named lanes from S. Fail if any listed module, dependency or UI directory is present.
Tool: git
Evidence: terminal-output(ls of the listed paths), terminal-output(cargo metadata dependency names), terminal-output(git diff --name-only on apps/observatory-app/ui/src)

### VAL-MAP-028: Red tests are committed before the code that turns them green in `wt/m0`
`git log --reverse --format='%h %s' $(git merge-base wt/m0 mission/observatory-v1)..wt/m0 -- crates/observatory-core/tests/mapping.rs crates/observatory-core/tests/store.rs crates/observatory-cli/tests/cli.rs` shows, for each of the seven M0 tests named in SPEC §3, a commit adding the test that precedes (in `--reverse` order) the first commit under `crates/observatory-core/src/mapping/v1/`, `crates/observatory-core/src/store/` or `crates/observatory-cli/src/inspect.rs` that makes it pass; the worker's tool-call log under `build-log/<date>/*.jsonl` contains a `cargo test` call whose output has `test result: FAILED` for that test before the green run (rule 1; SPEC §3 common). Every commit on the range carries the trailer `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`, and `git reflog`/`git log` show no amend, reset or force-push (rule 12). Fail if any test first appears in the same commit as, or after, its implementation, or if no red run is logged.
Tool: git
Evidence: terminal-output(git log --reverse over the range with paths), file(build-log/<date>/<session>.jsonl lines with "test result: FAILED")

### VAL-MAP-029: `make check` exits 0 in the M0 worktree
`make check` in `<repo>` (network available for `check-links`) exits 0, running `check-docs check-links check-workflows check-file-size check-todos check-decisions-index check-secrets fmt-check lint test deny replay-fixtures` in that order; `lint` is `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`. Paste the exit code and the `test result:` lines of `make test`. Fail on any non-zero sub-target.

### VAL-MAP-030: Fixture files are exempt from the 200 KB limit and every other tracked file is under it
`make check-file-size` (`MAX_FILE_KB=200`, `scripts/check-file-size.sh`) exits 0 in `<repo>`. `git ls-files | grep -v -E '^(fixtures/streams/|build-log/|Cargo.lock$)' | grep -v -E '\.(png|webp|mp4)$' | xargs wc -c | sort -n | tail -3` shows every listed file at or under 204800 bytes, including `docs/decisions/D-0NN-mapping-v1.md` and `crates/observatory-core/src/mapping/v1/kinds.rs`. Files under `fixtures/streams/` (the `.jsonl`, `.children/*.jsonl`, `.settings.json`, `.events.json`, `.capture.json`) may exceed 200 KB; record their sizes with `wc -c`. Fail if `check-file-size` exits non-zero or any non-exempt file is over 204800 bytes.

Evidence: terminal-output(make check-file-size exit code), terminal-output(wc -c largest non-exempt files), terminal-output(wc -c fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0*)

## board.md
## Area: M1 — Board in replay and attach (milestone m1)

Sources: `planning-notes.md` decisions 4 and 5; `architecture.md` §4.3, §7, §11, §14, §17; `SPEC.md` §3 "Common" and "M1", §5.5, §5.8, §6; PRD §7 (lane names), §8, FR-B1..B7, FR-D1, FR-A1..A4, FR-L1, FR-L2, FR-L4, §12 go/no-go; D-002; D-008; `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`.

Surfaces and preconditions:

- Browser host (primary interactive surface, planning note 4): `trunk serve --config apps/observatory-app/ui/Trunk.toml --port 3141 --open false` from the `wt/m1` worktree, driven by `agent-browser --session <validator-name>` (at most 3 sessions per `trunk serve`, SPEC §5.8). The fixture is opened through the file picker.
- M0 fixture: `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl` with `.capture.json`, `.settings.json` and `.children/`. S fixture for a non-zero unknown count: `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl`.
- CLI oracle: `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay <fixture>` (one line per event, last line `unknown events: N`) and `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- inspect <event-id>` (exact raw bytes).
- Tauri window (`make app-dev`): smoke check only (process alive, `Running .../debug/observatory-app` log line with no panic, `com.apple.WebKit` ESTABLISHED connections on 3141, System Events lists the process); one owner screenshot with the display unlocked at integration. Exactly one `trunk` owns 3141 at a time: stop the standalone `trunk serve` before `make app-dev`.
- Attach runs only in the Tauri window (the browser backend has no watcher). Live board state during attach is evidenced by the shell's tracing log lines (`session_discovered`, `events_appended` batches with timestamps) plus the owner screenshot; the validator cannot drive the Tauri webview. A temporary config (`OBSERVATORY_CONFIG=<tmp>/config.toml` with `[ingest].factory_sessions_dir` pointing at a temp directory) is used for the scripted attach cases so `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written.
- Nine lane names, PRD §7 order: `Intent`, `Orchestrator`, `Workers`, `Validators, scrutiny`, `Validators, user testing`, `Integration`, `Human`, `Outside`, `Time, Waste, Cost and models`.
- Six filters, FR-B5: milestone, feature, role, model, validation state, gate state.

### VAL-BOARD-001: Browser host serves the UI with no console errors at load
Start `trunk serve --config apps/observatory-app/ui/Trunk.toml --port 3141 --open false` in `wt/m1`; wait until `curl -sf http://localhost:3141/` returns 200 (cold build measured at 55.94 s). `agent-browser open http://localhost:3141` succeeds, `agent-browser snapshot` lists the app's `<main>` content (a library view or an "open a capture" control), and `agent-browser console` and `agent-browser errors` are both empty. Fail if the page is blank, if the snapshot shows only the trunk live-reload shell, or if either console list is non-empty.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: terminal-output(trunk serve ready line and curl status), snapshot(app-shell), console-errors, screenshot(app-shell)

### VAL-BOARD-002: Mission library lists past captures with name, date and event count only
On the browser surface before opening a capture, the mission library view lists each known capture as a row with three visible fields: name, date, event count (FR-L4; SPEC M1: headline metrics arrive with M5). For the M0 fixture row the event count equals the number of event lines printed by `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl` (all lines except the final `unknown events: N`). Fail if a cost, waste or cycle column is shown in M1, or if the count differs from the CLI.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(library-rows), terminal-output(cli replay line count)

### VAL-BOARD-003: Opening the M0 fixture through the file picker loads the board in Replay mode
Use `agent-browser` to select `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl` (and its `.children/*.jsonl` and `.settings.json` files when the picker accepts several files; record which files were loaded) in the file picker. The board view replaces the library, the mission name shown equals `mission_name` in `2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.capture.json` (`observatory-v1`), the mode indicator reads Replay, and the displayed event count equals the CLI replay event count for the same set of files. Fail if the board does not appear within 10 s of the file selection or if the counts differ.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(board-loaded-header), terminal-output(cli replay event count), screenshot(board-m0)

### VAL-BOARD-004: Nine lanes render with the PRD names in PRD order
With the M0 fixture open, the board shows exactly nine lane headers, left to right: `Intent`, `Orchestrator`, `Workers`, `Validators, scrutiny`, `Validators, user testing`, `Integration`, `Human`, `Outside`, `Time, Waste, Cost and models`. Fail on any missing, extra, renamed or reordered lane. Lanes 8 and 9 may be empty (no GitHub in M1; metrics arrive with M5) but their headers must be present.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(lane-names), screenshot(board-m0)

### VAL-BOARD-005: Each milestone card sits in the lane of its most recent open activity
For each milestone card on the board (one card per milestone defined in the capture's plan), compute from the CLI replay output the lane of the last event for that milestone whose kind is open activity (any lane 2–6 kind that is not a `*.done`, `*.passed`, `*.merged`, `*.finished` kind, or a lane 7/8 kind awaiting someone, per `core::view::card_lane`). The card is rendered in exactly that lane (FR-B1). Record a table card → expected lane → rendered lane. Fail if any card differs or if any milestone defined in the capture has no card.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(card-lanes), terminal-output(cli replay last open event per milestone), screenshot(board-m0)

### VAL-BOARD-006: Workers lane shows one sub-lane per worker by default
With the M0 fixture open, lane 3 `Workers` is divided into sub-lanes, one per worker child session present in the capture (the sessions with `role = worker` in `2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.capture.json` `sessions[]`). Each sub-lane header names its worker (tag or session id). Fail if the number of sub-lanes differs from the number of worker sessions in the capture header or if two workers share a sub-lane (FR-B2).
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(worker-sublanes-per-worker), terminal-output(capture.json worker session count)

### VAL-BOARD-007: Per-worker / per-feature toggle regroups lane 3 and toggles back
Click the lane-3 grouping toggle. The sub-lane headers switch from worker names to feature names (one per feature named by the mission plan in the capture), and the same lane-3 events are present (count unchanged). Click again: the per-worker grouping from VAL-BOARD-006 is restored exactly. Fail if the event count in lane 3 changes across the toggle or if the toggle does not return to the original grouping (FR-B2).
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(worker-sublanes-per-feature), snapshot(worker-sublanes-per-worker-restored), screenshot(toggle-per-feature)

### VAL-BOARD-008: The six FR-B5 filters are present
The filter bar offers exactly these six controls: milestone, feature, role, model, validation state, gate state. Fail if any of the six is missing. (Extra filters are a non-blocking finding, not a failure.)
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(filter-controls)

### VAL-BOARD-009: Milestone and feature filters narrow the board to the selected scope
Select one milestone (for example `m0`) in the milestone filter: only that milestone's card remains and every event rendered in lanes 1–7 belongs to that milestone or its features (cross-check the `milestone_id` column of the CLI replay output). Clear it, then select one feature id present in the capture in the feature filter: only the card of the milestone owning that feature remains, lane 3 shows only the sub-lane(s) carrying that feature's events, and the rendered event count equals the number of CLI replay lines with that `feature_id`. Clearing the filter restores the full card set from VAL-BOARD-005. Fail if another card or another feature's events stay visible under either filter, or if the clear does not restore the board.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(filter-milestone-applied), snapshot(filter-feature-applied), snapshot(filter-cleared), terminal-output(cli replay milestone and feature counts)

### VAL-BOARD-010: Role filter keeps only events of that role
Select `worker` in the role filter. The rendered events are only those whose role is Worker (the CLI replay `role` column); lanes 1, 2, 4 and 5 show no events; the agent panel, if it honours the filter, lists only worker sessions. Repeat with `scrutiny_validator`: only lane 4 and that validator's lane-3 `subagent.spawned`/`subagent.finished` events remain. Fail if an event of another role is visible under either selection.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(filter-role-worker), snapshot(filter-role-scrutiny), terminal-output(cli replay role counts)

### VAL-BOARD-011: Model filter keeps only events attributed to that model
Select `claude-sonnet-5-5` in the model filter. Only events whose `model` equals `claude-sonnet-5-5` remain, and the count equals the CLI replay lines with that model. Select `claude-fable-5.1`: only orchestrator-session events remain. Fail if an event with a different model or with no model stays visible when a model is selected.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(filter-model-sonnet), snapshot(filter-model-fable), terminal-output(cli replay model counts)

### VAL-BOARD-012: Validation-state and gate-state filters narrow by card badge
Select `RED` in the validation-state filter: only cards whose validation badge is RED (an open blocking finding or failed scenario at end of replay) remain; select `GREY`: only not-yet-validated cards remain; with `GREEN` the remaining cards all show GREEN. For the gate-state filter, selecting `pending` keeps every card (no PR exists for the M0 capture, PRD §8.1), and selecting any other gate state leaves no card. Fail if a card whose badge does not match the selected value stays visible.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(filter-validation-red), snapshot(filter-gate-pending), snapshot(filter-gate-other-empty)

### VAL-BOARD-013: Scrubbing back to a timestamp reproduces the CLI replay prefix
Pick `T` = the `at` of the median event line in the CLI replay output. Move the replay scrubber to `T`. The board shows only events with `at <= T` (rendered event count equals the number of CLI lines with `at <= T`), and each card's lane equals the lane of its most recent open activity among those lines (recompute as in VAL-BOARD-005 on the prefix). Fail if any event after `T` is visible or any card lane differs from the prefix computation (FR-B6, `scrubber_replays_to_a_timestamp`).
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(scrubbed-to-T), terminal-output(cli replay prefix count and card lanes at T), screenshot(scrubber-at-T)

### VAL-BOARD-014: Scrubbing forward to the end restores the full board
From the position of VAL-BOARD-013, move the scrubber to the end. The board is identical to the end-of-replay state of VAL-BOARD-005: same card lanes, same rendered event count, same tray count. Fail on any difference between the two snapshots.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(scrubbed-to-end), snapshot(card-lanes)

### VAL-BOARD-015: Filters and the scrubber compose
Apply the role filter `worker` (VAL-BOARD-010), then scrub to `T` from VAL-BOARD-013. The board shows only Worker events with `at <= T` (count equals the CLI lines satisfying both conditions). Then scrub back to the end: the role filter is still applied (no non-worker event appears). Fail if scrubbing clears the filter or if the filter clears the scrub position.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(filter-plus-scrub), snapshot(filter-kept-after-scrub-end), terminal-output(cli replay worker lines at T)

### VAL-BOARD-016: Unmapped tray count equals the CLI unknown count on the M0 fixture
With the M0 fixture open at end of replay, the unmapped tray shows the count `0`, and `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl` ends with `unknown events: 0` (SPEC M0 gate). ## host-control.md
## Area: M2 — Host (milestone m2)

Sources: `planning-notes.md` (decisions 4, 5, 8), `architecture.md` §4.5 RpcSource, §7 Tauri commands
(`host_launch`, `host_control`), §14, §17; `SPEC.md` §3 "Common", "M2 — Host", §5.8, §6; PRD FR-L3,
FR-A3, §13 M2 row; `docs/runbooks/fix-cycle.md` (the `droid exec` flag names per role);
`config/observatory.example.toml`. Worktree: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/m2`
on branch `wt/m2`.

Surfaces. The Tauri window is the only surface that can spawn the child process. Per planning decision 4
it is a smoke check (app process alive, `Running .../debug/observatory-app` log line, `com.apple.WebKit`
connections to port 3141, System Events lists the app); the oracles for what happens inside it are the
CLI (`observatory-cli replay|inspect`), `sqlite3` on `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite`, the spool
`~/.droid-observatory/hosted/<launch-id>.jsonl`, the app's tracing log, `ps`, and the hosted mission's own
session JSONL under `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/`. The browser host (`trunk serve --port 3141`,
`agent-browser --session <name>`, at most 3 sessions) renders the launch screen for form-level checks.
The scratch mission is a tiny mission file run on a scratch directory inside the `m2` worktree
(SPEC §3 M2 acceptance). Numbers below come from SPEC §5.5/§5.8 and `config/observatory.example.toml`.

### VAL-HOST-001: Launch screen shows the FR-L3 fields
In the browser host at `http://localhost:3141`, open the Launch screen. An `agent-browser snapshot` lists one input or select for each of these eleven fields: repo, mission file, mission branch name, orchestrator model, worker model, validator model, orchestrator reasoning effort, worker reasoning effort, validator reasoning effort, autonomy, budget (optional). Pass when all eleven are present and labelled; fail when any one is missing.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot text with the eleven field labels, screenshot `launch-fields.png`

### VAL-HOST-002: Model fields default to the `[mission]` config values
In the browser host, the Launch screen's three model fields are pre-filled with `[mission].orchestrator_model = "claude-fable-5.1"`, `[mission].worker_model = "claude-sonnet-5-5"`, `[mission].validator_model = "claude-opus-5-5"` (`config/observatory.example.toml`, D-006), and no model value is hard-coded in the UI crate (`grep -rn "claude-" apps/observatory-app/ui/src` returns zero lines). Pass when the three pre-filled values match the config defaults and the grep is empty.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot with the three model values, grep output

### VAL-HOST-003: Required fields refuse an empty Launch
In the browser host, for each of repo, mission file and mission branch name in turn: leave that one field empty, fill the others, click Launch. A validation message naming the empty field appears and the screen stays on the form. Pass when each of the three empty fields produces its own message; fail when any empty field is accepted or the message does not name the field.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: three snapshots with the message text, screenshot per field

### VAL-HOST-004: Budget is optional
In the Tauri window, fill repo, mission file and mission branch name, leave budget empty, click Launch. The launch proceeds: a new `~/.droid-observatory/hosted/<launch-id>.jsonl` spool file appears and `ps -axo pid,ppid,pgid,args | grep '[d]roid exec'` shows the child. Pass when both appear with budget empty; fail when the empty budget blocks the launch.
Tool: tauri-smoke
Evidence: `ls -l ~/.droid-observatory/hosted/`, ps line pasted, app log excerpt of `host_launch`

### VAL-HOST-005: Launch spawns the exact `droid exec` command on the scratch directory
After VAL-HOST-004, `ps -axo pid,ppid,pgid,args | grep '[d]roid exec'` shows one process whose arguments contain `droid exec --mission --input-format stream-jsonrpc --output-format stream-jsonrpc` and `-f <mission file>`, with `--model`, `--worker-model`, `--validator-model`, `--reasoning-effort`, `--worker-reasoning-effort`, `--validator-reasoning-effort` and the autonomy flag (`--auto <level>`) equal to the values entered on the form; `lsof -p <pid> | grep cwd` shows the scratch directory inside `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/m2`. Pass when every flag matches the form and the cwd is inside the worktree.
Tool: shell
Evidence: ps line pasted, lsof cwd line pasted, the form values used

### VAL-HOST-006: Tauri window passes the smoke set while hosting
With the hosted mission running, the four smoke items hold at the same time: the `observatory-app` process is alive (`ps -p <pid>`), the dev log contains the `Running .../debug/observatory-app` line, `lsof -iTCP:3141 -sTCP:ESTABLISHED` lists `com.apple.WebKit` connections, and `osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to get name of every process'` lists the app. Pass when all four hold; fail on any missing item.
Tool: tauri-smoke
Evidence: ps line, log line, lsof lines, osascript output

### VAL-HOST-007: Hosted stdout is spooled verbatim to the architecture path
The spool `~/.droid-observatory/hosted/<launch-id>.jsonl` grows while the child runs; every line parses as one JSON object (`jq -c . <spool> >/dev/null` exits 0 with no error); the file holds only child stdout (no stderr text). When the hosted mission ends, `wc -l <spool>` equals `sqlite3 ~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite "SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT byte_offset) FROM events WHERE source='rpc' AND path='<spool>'"`. Pass when jq exits 0 and the two counts are equal.
Tool: sqlite3
Evidence: `wc -l` output, sqlite3 output, jq exit code

### VAL-HOST-008: RPC events map to the same lane events as the session file
`cargo test -p observatory-core --test rpc rpc_events_map_to_the_same_lane_events_as_the_session_file` passes in `wt/m2`. Pass on exit code 0 with the test listed as `ok`.
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: test output pasted with the test name and `test result: ok`

### VAL-HOST-009: Hosted events carry `SourcePtr::Rpc` and mapping version `v1`
After a hosted run, `sqlite3 ... "SELECT DISTINCT source, mapping_version FROM events WHERE path='<spool>'"` returns exactly one row `rpc|v1`, and `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE source='rpc' AND (byte_offset IS NULL OR byte_len IS NULL)` returns 0. Pass when both hold.
Tool: sqlite3
Evidence: both query outputs pasted

### VAL-HOST-010: Each hosted event renders within 1 s
With the hosted mission running, for every spool line the interval between the line's arrival (the app log's tail-read entry for that `byte_offset`, or the file mtime at the poll that read it) and the `events_appended` flush that contains its event is under 1000 ms (`[ingest].jsonl_poll_ms` 500 plus `[ui].event_batch_ms` 100 give the headroom). Pass when the maximum interval over the run is < 1000 ms; the p50/p95/max are pasted.
Tool: shell
Evidence: p50/p95/max pasted from the log analysis, log excerpt for the maximum

### VAL-HOST-011: Pause request is written as JSON-RPC and acknowledged (test)
`cargo test -p observatory-core --test rpc pause_request_is_written_as_jsonrpc_and_acknowledged` passes in `wt/m2`: the encoded request has `jsonrpc: "2.0"`, a numeric `id`, the pause method name, and the acknowledgement is the response with the same `id`. Pass on exit code 0 with the test listed as `ok`.
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: test output pasted

## gate.md
## Area: M4 — Mission branch, gate and fix loop (milestone m4)

Sources: `planning-notes.md` decisions 6 and 7 (read-only PAT; Actions runs + commit statuses, never
check-runs; owner merges, app shows the 403 cleanly), `architecture.md` §4.6, §6, §7, §8, §11, §15,
`SPEC.md` §3 Common and M4, §5.9, §7, §8, PRD FR-G1..G8, FR-B3, FR-B4, §7 lanes 6 and 8, §8.1, §13 M4
row, §14 risk row, `docs/decisions/D-007-main-ruleset.md`, `.github/workflows/mission-branch.yml`.

Test target (SPEC §3 M4, B-007): repository `dctellya/droid-observatory`; long-lived `demo/base`
created from `mission/observatory-v1`; ruleset `demo-gate` on `refs/heads/demo/base`; PRs from
`demo/*` into `demo/base`; `.github/workflows/demo-gate.yml` red when label `demo:red` is present.
Never `main`, never ruleset `main-gate` (id 25636994, D-007).

Surface. The GitHub poll (`GitHubSource`, `Forge`) runs only in the Tauri shell: the UI crate depends
on `observatory-core` with `default-features = false`, so the `github` feature is not compiled to wasm
and the browser host (`trunk serve --port 3141`, `BrowserBackend`, file picker, no store) has no live
gate data (architecture §2, §7). Live gate assertions therefore use the Tauri window started with
`make app-dev` (smoke check per planning note 4), its stdout captured to a file (the "app log"),
the store `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite`, and `gh api` / `gh pr` as the oracle. The browser
host contributes only the view-level `cargo test` assertions. Pressing Merge and reading dialog text
in the Tauri window is done by a human at the keyboard with the display unlocked (planning note 4);
the owner's integration screenshot is the visual evidence. Where the app does not log GitHub request
URLs (method, URL, status, no headers; architecture §12 logs status and URL on error), VAL-GATE-018,
-019, -020 and -031 are unverifiable and the validator reports that as a blocking gap.

Configuration for the live run (pasted into the report): `[github].repo = "dctellya/droid-observatory"`,
`[github].target_branch = "demo/base"`, `[github].merge_policy = "auto"` (except VAL-GATE-024),
`[github].poll_interval_s = 30`, the observed mission's branch resolving to `demo/red-1` through
`[mission].branch_pattern`. Token: keychain `droid-observatory/github-token` (read-only PAT, planning
note 6); `GITHUB_TOKEN` must be unset in the shell that starts the app so the keychain path is exercised.

### VAL-GATE-001: demo/base exists and descends from the mission branch
`gh api repos/dctellya/droid-observatory/branches/demo/base` returns 200, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha of mission/observatory-v1 at demo/base creation> origin/demo/base` exits 0 (the creation commit sha is pasted from the orchestrator's log). Fail if the branch is missing or was not created from the mission branch.
Tool: gh

## metrics.md
## Area: M5 — Time, waste, cost (milestone m5)

Sources: SPEC.md §3 "Common" and "M5 — Time, waste, cost", §5.5–§5.7, §5.9, §6, §8; PRD v0.6 §7 lane 9, §10.1–10.5, FR-M1..M7, FR-D2..D6, FR-L4; architecture.md §9–§12; D-004, D-010; `config/observatory.example.toml`; `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`; `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`; planning notes (decisions 2 and 4 binding). Worktree for the milestone: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/m5` on branch `wt/m5`. Repository root below is `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`; the fixture is `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl`.

Closed lists used throughout (SPEC §5.6):

- Waste causes (8): `waiting_human_question`, `waiting_human_permission`, `waiting_merge`, `waiting_validation`, `rework`, `retry_failure`, `idle_queued`, `idle_unscheduled`.
- Rework causes (4): `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate`.
- Time states (6, PRD §10.1): Active, Waiting on human (sub-causes question, permission, merge), Waiting on validation, Retry and failure, Idle queued, Idle unscheduled.
- Details tabs added in M5 (5): Cost and waste (FR-D6), Review notes (FR-D2), Validation criteria (FR-D3), Commits and integration (FR-D4), Gate (FR-D5).
- Lane-9 chart types (3): stacked bars, timeline, sparkline.

Precondition (SPEC §3 M5 "Oracle", architecture §17): the owner's reference CSV must exist before any M5 metrics work starts. VAL-METRIC-001 states it; if it fails, the stall flag goes up and the remaining VAL-METRIC assertions are not evaluated until the owner supplies the file.

### VAL-METRIC-001: Reference CSV is present at the M4→M5 boundary
`reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv` is tracked on `mission/observatory-v1` at the M4→M5 boundary and its first line is exactly the 20-column header `scope,id,name,cycle_s,first_pass_active_s,rework_s,waste_waiting_human_question_s,waste_waiting_human_permission_s,waste_waiting_merge_s,waste_waiting_validation_s,waste_rework_s,waste_retry_failure_s,waste_idle_queued_s,waste_idle_unscheduled_s,rework_windows,tokens_input,tokens_output,tokens_cache_read,tokens_cache_write,cost_usd,price_table`. Pass: the file is tracked and the header matches byte for byte. Fail: file absent or header differs; the M5 integration feature raises the stall flag and asks the owner (SPEC §3 M5 "Missing at the M4→M5 boundary = stall flag, human input").
Tool: git
Evidence: `git -C /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory ls-files reports/reference/` output, first line of the CSV, boundary report line stating present or stall flag raised

### VAL-METRIC-002: CLI metrics --csv prints the column contract
`cargo run -p observatory-cli -- metrics fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl --csv` exits 0 and prints RFC 4180 CSV whose header equals the 20-column line in VAL-METRIC-001 and whose data rows have `scope` in {`feature`, `milestone`}, every `*_s` column an integer number of seconds, every `tokens_*` column an integer, `cost_usd` a decimal, and `price_table` equal to `2026-10-22`. Pass: header identical, no row violates any field rule. Fail: any extra, missing or reordered column, or any field outside its rule.
Tool: cli
Evidence: exit code, pasted header line, row count, pasted first feature row and first milestone row

### VAL-METRIC-003: Metrics match the owner's reference spreadsheet within tolerance (hard gate)
`cargo test -p observatory-core --test oracle` runs `metrics_match_reference_spreadsheet_within_tolerance()` green: for every row of `reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv` keyed by (`scope`, `id`) the engine produces a row where each duration column differs by at most 1 s, each token column by at most 1 token, `cost_usd` by at most 0.01 USD, `rework_windows` is equal, and `price_table` is equal; no reference row is missing from the engine output and no engine row is missing from the reference. Pass: test passes and the independent `diff` of the CLI `--csv` output against the reference shows only differences inside the tolerance. Fail: any row outside tolerance, any row missing on either side, or the test is skipped or ignored. This assertion is the milestone's hard gate (SPEC §3 M5 "Gate").
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: `cargo test -p observatory-core --test oracle` output with `test result: ok`, pasted per-column maximum deviations, `diff` of CLI CSV vs reference

### VAL-METRIC-004: CLI metrics --json prints a MetricsReport consistent with the CSV
`cargo run -p observatory-cli -- metrics fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl --json` exits 0 and prints one JSON document (`MetricsReport`) that parses, and for each feature and milestone row of the `--csv` output the same (`scope`, `id`) entry exists in the JSON with equal `cycle_s`, `first_pass_active_s`, `rework_s`, `rework_windows`, token counts and `cost_usd`, and a `price_table` field equal to `2026-10-22`. Pass: JSON parses and every CSV row has an equal JSON counterpart. Fail: parse error or any disagreement between the two outputs.
Tool: cli

Scope: flows that span two or more milestones of `s`, `m0`, `m1`, `m2`, `m3`, `m4`, `m5` and

unless absolute. The M0 capture is `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl` with its
