### VAL-CROSS-001: Clean clone replays the skeleton snapshot with the README commands (S)
From a fresh `git clone user@example.invalid:dctellya/droid-observatory.git` into an empty temporary directory, checked out at the `s` integration commit on `mission/observatory-v1`, the README sequence `make doctor`, `make hooks`, `make check`, then `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` runs with every command exiting 0 and the replay's last stdout line matching `^unknown events: [0-9]+$` (N > 0 allowed at S). Fail if any command exits non-zero, `make doctor` reports a missing required tool, or the last line differs (SPEC §3 S exit criterion, RULES rule 5).
Tool: shell
Evidence: clone path, `make doctor` output, `make check` exit code, replay stdout last line, commit sha of the clone

### VAL-CROSS-002: Clean clone builds the UI and reaches the board (M1)
On the same kind of fresh clone at the `m1` integration commit, the README command for the Trunk build (`trunk build --config apps/observatory-app/ui/Trunk.toml`, or the exact README wording at M1) exits 0, `trunk serve --config apps/observatory-app/ui/Trunk.toml --port 3141 --open false` serves `http://localhost:3141`, and opening the M0 capture through the file picker renders nine lanes named in PRD §7 order with at least one milestone card. Fail if the build fails, the page shows a console error, or fewer than nine lanes render (SPEC §3 M1 gate "Trunk/WASM build succeeds from a clean checkout with the README command"; architecture §17 M1 go/no-go).
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: `trunk build` exit code and wall time (pasted), agent-browser snapshot of the board, console errors output (expected empty), clone commit sha

### VAL-CROSS-003: Dogfooding starts at M1 integration: the mission's own orchestrator session is on the board
With `make app-dev` running after the `m1` integration (`current` → `observatory-wt/m2`), the orchestrator session of this mission (the root `.jsonl` under `~/.factory/sessions/-home-user-code-EllyaOrg-projects-dalimaray-droid-observatory/` with no `callingSessionId`, modified within `[ingest].startup_scan_hours` = 24) is listed by `list_sessions` and attached without the validator selecting it by hand (startup scan), with its card named by the first `--tag` or, absent a tag, its session id. Fail if the session is missing from the list, needs a manual attach, or is named otherwise (SPEC §3 M1 exit criterion; architecture §4.3; FR-L1).
Tool: tauri-smoke
Evidence: `ls -lt ~/.factory/sessions/-home-user-code-EllyaOrg-projects-dalimaray-droid-observatory/*.jsonl | head`, `list_sessions` output or the app log line naming the attached session id, owner's unlocked-display screenshot path

### VAL-CROSS-004: Each later milestone's live events appear on the dogfooded board within 1 s (M2, M3, M4, M5)
At each of the `m2`, `m3`, `m4` and `m5` validation passes, with the board attached to the mission's own session files, the validator records the `timestamp` of one new line appended to a watched session file (`tail -n1 <file> | jq -r .timestamp`, or the file mtime from `stat -f %Fm`) and the wall-clock time at which the corresponding event is visible on the board; the difference is below 1000 ms for each of the four milestones. Fail if any of the four measurements is ≥ 1000 ms or the event never appears (SPEC §1 "must prove" 1; SPEC §3 M1 exit criterion "the rest of this mission is watched by attaching to its own session files").
Tool: shell

## 3. Milestones

Seven milestones on the board of the build: the walking skeleton `S` first (rule 2), then
`M0`–`M5` in PRD §13 order. PRD §13 counts six; the seventh is the skeleton rule 2 requires, so
the PRD count is superseded here (rule 8). A milestone is integrated into the mission branch, never
shipped. The spec itself is not a milestone: it is approved before the mission starts.

**B-010 settled: skeleton before M0, and the capture is this mission.** Rule 2 wants the thinnest
end-to-end slice first; PRD §13 wants M0 to freeze the mapping before M1–M5 are planned in detail.
Both hold because the capture needs no extra mission: the moment the owner runs the §2 command, the
orchestrator's session JSONL is growing under `~/.factory/sessions/`, and the skeleton's workers
and validators add child sessions for every role. `S` replays a snapshot of that file through a
mapper that knows nothing yet (every line is `unknown.event`, counted). `M0` snapshots the same
sessions again at `S` integration, now with all four roles present, freezes it as the fixture,
and drives the unknown count to zero. The optional B-009 pre-capture is not needed; a small
sample-repo mission (PRD §13 M0) is the fallback only if role identification cannot be established
from this mission's own files.

**Common to every milestone.**

- Tests first (rule 1): each feature begins with a red test committed in the worktree; the
  scrutiny validator checks that the red run exists in the worker's log.
- Acceptance commands are the ones in §6 and `make check`; counts are pasted, not estimated.
- Exit needs: `make check` green on the mission branch after integration, `mission-checks` green
  on the push, zero blocking findings open, §9/§10 rows written, README/BACKLOG/decisions index
  updated (rule 16), `reports/usage/<m>.md` and `reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json` added
  (B-015), and no `unknown.event` on the capture if the milestone adds a source (rule 18).
- Must not touch: `main`, another milestone's worktree, `rust-toolchain.toml` without a decision,
  the shared files (§2), the ruleset on `main`.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/streams/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl` is the orchestrator session; its child
  sessions live in `fixtures/streams/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.children/<session-id>.jsonl` with the
  `.settings.json` beside each. A fixture is committed only after `gitleaks detect --no-git` on the
  directory is clean and a reviewer has read it; raw lines may carry tool output.

### S — Walking skeleton

- **Outcome.** Cargo workspace with `crates/observatory-core`, `crates/observatory-cli`,
  `apps/observatory-app`; the canonical `Event` (PRD appendix A) with `EventKind::Unknown`;
  `observatory-cli replay <file>` reads a session JSONL and prints one line per event and the
  summary `unknown events: N`; the Tauri window starts and shows nine empty lanes with their
  names; `Cargo.lock` committed; `cargo deny` configured against `deny.toml`.
- **Tests green.** `replay_counts_every_line_of_a_capture()`,
  `unknown_event_keeps_raw_type_and_byte_offset()`, `event_round_trips_through_serde()`,
  `lanes_are_nine_in_prd_order()`, `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file()`,
  `every_event_carries_the_mapping_version()`.
- **Acceptance commands.** `make check`; `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay
  fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` (prints `unknown events: N`, N > 0 allowed);
  `make app-dev` opens the window (screenshot in the validator report).
- **Gate.** `make check`, `mission-checks` green, `make deny` green, coverage reported (not yet
  enforced, §6).
- **Exit criterion.** The skeleton replays its own snapshot end to end from a clean clone with the
  README commands (rule 5); B-016 (`release.yml` checks the workspace version against the tag) is
  wired because `Cargo.toml` now exists; B-005 and B-014 jobs are in `mission-branch.yml`.
- **Must not touch.** No mapping beyond `Unknown`, no store, no metrics, no board interaction.

### M0 — Stream capture and mapping

- **Outcome.** `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl` (+ children) frozen from this
  mission's sessions at `S` integration; `mapping::v1` from raw lines to PRD §7 kinds, selected by
  the Droid version in the session `.settings.json`; confirmation of where `--tag`, child sessions,
  roles, feature and milestone ids are recorded (PRD §11.1 open items), written to
  `docs/decisions/` and `library` of the fixture; SQLite store with the pointer index (§5.3);
  `observatory-cli replay` and `inspect <event-id>` (prints the raw line by pointer).
- **Tests green.** Golden tests `mapping_v1_matches_golden_lane_events()` (fixture → expected
  `.events.json`), `every_prd_kind_present_in_capture_is_mapped()`, `unknown_count_is_zero_on_m0_capture()`,
  `child_sessions_attach_to_their_parent()`, `roles_resolve_for_orchestrator_worker_and_both_validators()`,
  `store_pointer_reads_back_the_exact_raw_line()`, `mapping_version_is_selected_by_droid_version()`.
- **Acceptance commands.** `make replay-fixtures`; `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay
  fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl` ends with `unknown events: 0`;
  `cargo test -p observatory-core --test mapping`.
- **Gate.** All of the common gate plus `unknown events: 0` on the M0 capture (hard).
- **Exit criterion.** The mapping is frozen (`mapping::v1`, versioned by Droid 0.247.x); PRD §7
  kinds that do not occur in the capture are listed in `docs/decisions/D-0NN-mapping-v1.md` as
  "defined, not observed". **This is the gate for planning M1–M5 in detail** (PRD §13).
- **Must not touch.** No UI beyond the empty lanes; no git/GitHub adapters; no metrics.

### M1 — Board in replay and attach

- **Outcome.** Board with nine lanes and milestone cards positioned by current lane (FR-B1), worker
  sub-lanes with the per-worker/per-feature toggle (FR-B2), filters (FR-B5), replay scrubber
  (FR-B6), unmapped tray (FR-B7); Details with the Timeline tab (FR-D1) opening raw lines;
  agent panel (FR-A1..A4) with `model.changed` and `context.compacted` markers. Attach: `notify`
  watcher on `[ingest].factory_sessions_dir` paired with the `jsonl_poll_ms` poll, startup scan of
  files already growing, tail on growth, render within 1 s, name by `--tag` or session id
  (FR-L1); replay is the same adapter at end of file (FR-L2). Read-only scrub pass before display
  (B-006) for the obvious token shapes, read-only rendering regardless. Mission library listing
  past missions with headline metrics (FR-L4; headline metrics arrive with M5, until then the list
  shows name, date, event count).
- **Tests green.** `card_sits_in_lane_of_most_recent_open_activity()`, `scrubber_replays_to_a_timestamp()`,
  `unmapped_tray_count_equals_unknown_events()`, `watcher_sees_a_new_session_file_within_poll_interval()`,
  `tail_renders_appended_lines_in_order()`, `attach_latency_under_one_second_on_fixture_replayed_live()`
  (a test harness appends the fixture line by line with timestamps), `name_prefers_tag_over_session_id()`,
  `scrub_masks_known_token_shapes_without_altering_the_store()`.
- **Acceptance commands.** `make check`; `trunk serve --port 3141` (browser host of the UI for the
  validators, §6); `make app-dev`; a mission started in a terminal appears on the board, each event
  within 1 s, measured by the attach-latency test and by the validator's timestamps.
- **Gate.** Common gate plus the **Leptos go/no-go** (PRD §12): the board renders the M0 capture
  (nine lanes, cards positioned correctly, Details timeline open) with at most 3 worker sessions
  of rework after the first scrutiny pass, and the Trunk/WASM build succeeds from a clean checkout
  with the README command. Fail → switch the UI to Tauri + TypeScript for M2 onward, core and the
  Tauri command boundary unchanged, decision file, owner approval.
- **Exit criterion.** Dogfooding starts: the rest of this mission is watched by attaching to its
  own session files (PRD §13).
- **Must not touch.** No hosting, no control channel, no GitHub.

### M2 — Host

- **Outcome.** Launch screen (FR-L3): repo, mission file, mission branch name, models and
  reasoning effort per role, autonomy, optional budget; spawn `droid exec --mission
  --input-format stream-jsonrpc --output-format stream-jsonrpc`; `RpcSource` adapter; pause,
  message, answer over the input channel; live output per agent (FR-A3).
- **Tests green.** `rpc_events_map_to_the_same_lane_events_as_the_session_file()`,
  `pause_request_is_written_as_jsonrpc_and_acknowledged()`, `answer_routes_to_the_open_question_id()`,
  `host_and_attach_of_the_same_mission_agree_on_event_count()`, `child_process_is_reaped_on_window_close()`.
- **Acceptance commands.** `make check`; from the app launch a short mission on a scratch
  directory inside the worktree; events within 1 s; pause/message/answer reach the orchestrator and
  its reaction appears; the same mission attached from its JSONL shows the same lane events.
- **Gate.** Common gate; zero `unknown.event` on the hosted capture (new source, rule 18).
- **Exit criterion.** PRD §13 M2 validation satisfied with the pasted event counts.
- **Must not touch.** Lane-7 semantics beyond logging the three controls (M3), GitHub.

### M3 — Intervention

- **Outcome.** Every control is a lane-7 event with the human as actor (FR-H1..H4: pause/resume,
  message, answer and approve/deny, mark complete/skipped); stall flag at
  `[intervention].stall_threshold_min` with the matching runbook prompt (FR-H5, `docs/runbooks/`);
  no nudging under threshold (FR-H6).
- **Tests green.** `each_control_emits_one_lane7_event_with_actor_human()`,
  `stall_flag_raises_after_threshold_of_no_active_time()`, `stall_flag_suggests_the_matching_runbook()`,
  `no_alert_for_waits_under_threshold()`, `mark_skipped_relays_as_an_instruction_to_the_orchestrator()`.
- **Acceptance commands.** `make check`; each action against a hosted mission produces the lane-7
  event and the orchestrator reacts (pasted event ids).
- **Gate.** Common gate.
- **Exit criterion.** `docs/runbooks/stalled-mission.md` app steps replace the CLI steps (B-012
  "revise at M3").
- **Must not touch.** GitHub, metrics.

### M4 — Mission branch, gate, and fix loop

- **Outcome.** `GitSource`: mission branch, milestone worktrees, integration commits, fast-check
  runs → lane 6 (FR-G1, FR-G2). `GitHubSource` behind the `Forge` trait: PR detection for
  `<mission branch>` → `<target branch>` (target parameterised, not hard-coded `main`), check runs,
  required checks, reviews, rulesets, attestations (FR-G3); merge policy with rule attribution and
  the `[github].merge_policy` override (FR-G4); gate group and badge in lane 8 (FR-B3); Merge
  button with confirmation naming PR and target (FR-G5); `policy-merged` on detection (FR-G6);
  CI red → `fix` cycle on the affected card(s), same PR, return arc (FR-B4, FR-G7); completion on
  merge and branch-deletion detection (FR-G8).
- **Test target (B-007 decided, entry 19).** A demo branch pair in this repository: long-lived
  `demo/base` created by the orchestrator from the mission branch; a ruleset `demo-gate` on
  `refs/heads/demo/base` (PR required, required check `demo-gate`, no force push); PRs from
  `demo/*` into `demo/base`; `.github/workflows/demo-gate.yml` on `pull_request` to `demo/base`
  (types `opened, synchronize, labeled, unlabeled`) that fails when the label `demo:red` is present
  and passes otherwise. Deterministic red and green, no `main` involvement, no second repository.
  The ruleset is created with `gh api` under the owner's token; if the token lacks admin, the
  owner creates it at the M3→M4 boundary (a human input, §2). Demo branches `demo/*` are deleted
  after each run; `demo/base` stays as test infrastructure and is listed in the README.
- **Tests green.** `pr_for_mission_branch_is_detected_within_poll_interval()`,
  `red_required_check_opens_a_fix_cycle_on_the_affected_card()`, `fix_cycle_keeps_the_same_pr()`,
  `merge_button_shows_only_when_policy_is_human_and_checks_are_green()`, `rule_attribution_names_the_ruleset()`,
  `policy_merged_detected_without_human_action()`, `gate_command_runs_are_lane6_events_attributed_to_the_milestone()`,
  `target_branch_is_read_from_config_not_hardcoded()`.
- **Acceptance commands.** `make check`; `demo/red-1` PR with `demo:red` → check fails → card
  loops to lane 3 with cycle count 1; label removed → check passes → Merge visible → merge from the
  app → badge updates → `demo/red-1` deleted. All run ids and PR numbers pasted.
- **Gate.** Common gate; zero `unknown.event` from the git and GitHub sources (rule 18).
- **Exit criterion.** PRD §13 M4 validation satisfied on the demo pair; the decision file for the
  demo branch pair is written (the PRD §13 M4 row, §14 risk row and BACKLOG B-007 are already
  reworded in the spec PR, entry 19).
- **Must not touch.** The `main` ruleset, `main` itself, metrics.

### M5 — Time, waste, cost

- **Outcome.** Time-state engine (PRD §10.1), rework windows (§10.2), mission overhead (§10.3),
  cycle, waste, bottleneck, fix loops (§10.4), tokens and cost with the dated price table and
  credits when exposed (§10.5), budget meter (FR-M6), model comparison (FR-M7), CSV/JSON export,
  Details tabs Cost and waste (FR-D6), Review notes (FR-D2), Validation criteria (FR-D3), Commits
  and integration (FR-D4), Gate (FR-D5); lane 9 panel with SVG charts (stacked bars, timeline,
  sparkline); Grafana export of the §5.7 series behind `[telemetry].enabled`.
- **Oracle (B-008).** `reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv`, produced by the owner
  by hand from the M0 capture before M5 starts: per feature and per milestone, cycle seconds,
  first-pass active seconds, waste seconds by cause, rework windows, tokens by class, cost at
  `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`. Rounding tolerance: 1 s on durations, 1 token, 0.01 USD.
  Missing at the M4→M5 boundary = stall flag, human input (§2).
- **Tests green.** `time_states_partition_every_instant_exactly_once()`,
  `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`, `overlapping_windows_merge_on_one_feature()`,
  `unresolved_window_is_reported_at_mission_end()`, `first_pass_excludes_rework_windows()`,
  `overhead_is_reported_separately_unless_apportionment_is_equal()`,
  `metrics_match_reference_spreadsheet_within_tolerance()`, `cost_names_the_price_table_date()`,
  `exported_series_count_is_under_budget_on_worst_case_labels()`, `labels_outside_allowed_set_are_rejected()`,
  `telemetry_stays_off_without_keychain_item_and_ui_says_so()`.
- **Acceptance commands.** `make check`; `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- metrics
  fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl --csv` diffed against the reference within
  tolerance; with the keychain item present and `[telemetry].enabled = true`, series appear in the
  owner's Grafana stack with only the allowed labels (screenshot pasted).
- **Gate.** Common gate; oracle test green (hard).
- **Exit criterion.** All six "must prove" items of §1 hold; the orchestrator opens the single PR
  `mission/observatory-v1` → `main`, the `gate` runs, the human merges, the branch dies.
- **Must not touch.** Anything that changes the frozen mapping or the M0 fixture.

## 4. Versions

content.thinking:
Adding up the totals across all sections gives 287, and I need to cut this down to roughly 215–230 to hit a 20-25% reduction. Now I'm working through each area to decide what to trim, starting with SKEL.

For SKEL, several items duplicate mission-wide process assertions and should move to PROC instead: worktree identity, shared-file restrictions, red-before-green, commit conventions, and the `make check` requirement. I'm weighing whether the coverage-reporting item is S-specific enough to keep locally or whether it should also fold into a shared PROC coverage assertion.

For the "must not touch" scope checks, I'm deciding whether to fold them into a single PROC assertion listing per-milestone exclusions, though the fixture-hash-unchanged and behavior-specific parts may need to stay separate since they're actual behavioral checks rather than pure scope restrictions.

I'm now comparing the various "fixture hash unchanged" checks across SKEL-021, BOARD-021, METRIC-026, and CROSS-010 — recognizing these represent genuinely distinct observations (runtime read-only behavior versus cross-milestone freeze) that shouldn't be collapsed together despite the surface-level similarity in wording.

SKEL-030 and CROSS-001 are true duplicates too — keeping SKEL-030 at the area level and dropping CROSS-001. For BOARD-035 versus CROSS-002, the latter adds a "serve and reach board" observation; I'm inclined to fold that into BOARD-035 since it's basically the same go/no-go criterion from the spec just extended slightly.

## r3
### 5.7 Telemetry series budget (D-010, B-017)

Contract: OTLP `http/protobuf` to `https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp`; header
value only from the keychain item `droid-observatory/otlp-headers`; resource attributes
`service.name=droid-observatory`, `service.version`; labels only from `mission`, `milestone`,
`role`, `model`, `cause`; counters and histograms only; one mission exported at a time.

| Metric | Instrument | Labels | Cardinality (worst case) | Series |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `observatory.mission.cycle_seconds` | histogram, 6 buckets | `mission` | 1 × (6 + `+Inf` + `_sum` + `_count`) | 9 |
| `observatory.feature.cycle_seconds` | histogram, 5 buckets | `mission` | 1 × (5 + 3) | 8 |
| `observatory.waste_seconds` | counter | `mission`, `milestone`, `cause` | 8 milestones × 8 causes | 64 |
| `observatory.rework_windows` | counter | `mission`, `milestone`, `cause` | 8 × 4 | 32 |
| `observatory.fix_loops` | counter | `mission`, `milestone` | 8 | 8 |
| `observatory.tokens.{input,output,cache_read,cache_write}` | 4 counters | `mission`, `role`, `model` | 3 roles × 4 models = 12 pairs × 4 | 48 |
| `observatory.cost_usd` | counter | `mission`, `role`, `model` | 12 | 12 |
| `observatory.unknown_events` | counter | `mission` | 1 | 1 |
| **Total worst case** | | | | **182** |

Expected for this mission (7 milestones, 3 role×model pairs): 9 + 8 + 56 + 28 + 7 + 12 + 3 + 1 =
**124**. Both are strictly under 200. Why these shapes: the feature-cycle histogram carries no
`milestone` label because a histogram per milestone (7 series each) would cost 56 series for a
distribution the app already shows per card; waste and rework keep `milestone` because the budget
meter and the waste chart are read per card. Guards: the `milestone` label is bounded by
`max_milestone_labels` (the ninth and later milestones of any observed mission export as
`milestone="overflow"`); `role` is the closed `Role` enum; `model` beyond four distinct values per
mission exports as `model="other"`; the exporter refuses to start if its computed worst case for the
configured buckets and limits is not under `[telemetry].max_series`, and the test
`exported_series_count_is_under_budget_on_worst_case_labels()` pins the 182. Series of a previous
mission stop being written when the export target changes; `mission_switch_min_interval_min` keeps
the two sets from overlapping inside Grafana's active-series window. A `service.version` change
(release) re-keys the resource once; it is not a steady-state cost. CI telemetry stays deferred
(B-002). D-010 sized the shape at up to 6 milestones; this spec uses 8 label values because the
skeleton makes seven milestones and one `overflow` value bounds other missions. Still under 200.

## r0
### 5.5 Config keys with defaults

Everything in `config/observatory.example.toml` as committed (`[mission]`, `[ingest]`, `[github]`,
`[intervention]`, `[metrics]`, `[telemetry]`), with these additions the mission makes, each with
its reason in the file (rule 4):

| Key | Default | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `[ingest].max_watched_sessions` | 64 | Bounds file handles and tail threads on a laptop; beyond it the newest are watched and the UI says how many are not. |
| `[ingest].max_session_file_mb` | 512 | Larger files are indexed but tail reads warn; protects memory on runaway sessions. |
| `[ingest].tail_chunk_kb` | 1024 | Read size per tail step; one chunk per poll keeps latency under 1 s at typical mission output rates. |
| `[ui].event_batch_ms` | 100 | Shell→UI flush interval (§5.1). |
| `[ui].dev_port` | 3141 | `trunk serve` port for the browser host used by validators (§6); chosen outside common dev ranges, confirmed free at planning. |
| `[store].path` | `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite` | One index per user; raw lines stay where Droid wrote them. |
| `[telemetry].max_milestone_labels` | 8 | 7 named milestones of this mission plus one `overflow` value; bounds the `milestone` label for any observed mission (§5.7). |
| `[telemetry].mission_switch_min_interval_min` | 30 | The exported mission changes at most twice an hour, so two missions' series never count as active together (§5.7). |
| `[telemetry].buckets.mission_cycle_seconds` | `[3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 86400, 172800]` | Missions run hours to days. |
| `[telemetry].buckets.feature_cycle_seconds` | `[600, 1800, 3600, 7200, 14400]` | Features run minutes to hours. |

### 5.6 Metric definitions

By reference, not restated: time states PRD §10.1, rework windows §10.2, mission overhead §10.3,
cycle/waste/bottleneck/fix loops §10.4, cost §10.5. Closed cause lists used by the engine and the
exporter: **waste causes** `waiting_human_question`, `waiting_human_permission`, `waiting_merge`,
`waiting_validation`, `rework`, `retry_failure`, `idle_queued`, `idle_unscheduled` (8);
**rework causes** `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate` (4). Mission overhead is a
separate line in the app and is not exported (reason: it belongs to no card and D-010 has no label
for it). The CSV export has one row per feature with every §10.4 measure and the price-table date.

### 5.7 Telemetry series budget (D-010, B-017)

# Validation contract — mission `observatory-v1`

## Sources and precedence

This contract is synthesized from the seven area drafts in `contract-work/` (`skel.md`, `map.md`, `board.md`,
`host-control.md`, `gate.md`, `metrics.md`, `cross-process.md`). Where sources disagree the order is:
`planning-notes.md` (owner decisions after the spec, binding) > `SPEC.md` v0.2 > `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`
v0.6. `architecture.md` is the design reference: assertions whose only source is the architecture (file layouts,
log line names, config defaults not yet in `config/observatory.example.toml`, exact UI strings) are kept and
tagged `(source: architecture)` in their description; a worker who changes that design detail must change the
assertion through the orchestrator, not fail it silently. Numbers are the sources' numbers, pasted, never
estimated (RULES rule 7). Repository: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`; worktrees
`/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/<m>` on branch `wt/<m>` for `<m>` in `s`, `m0`,
`m1`, `m2`, `m3`, `m4`, `m5`; `<wt/m>` below means that worktree root.

## Evidence conventions

Each assertion ends with `Tool:` (one word from the vocabulary below) and `Evidence:` (a comma-separated list of
artifacts the validator attaches). Evidence items use these forms:

- `screenshot(<name>)` — a PNG taken by `agent-browser screenshot` (browser host) or, for the Tauri window, the
  owner's unlocked-display screenshot named `owner-screenshot(<path>)`.
- `snapshot(<name>)` — the text of `agent-browser snapshot` (accessibility tree) at that moment.
- `console-errors` — the output of `agent-browser console` and `agent-browser errors` (expected empty unless stated).
- `terminal-output(<command or what>)` — the pasted stdout/stderr and exit code of a shell command.
- `gh-output(<what>)` — pasted `gh` / `gh api` output with the command that produced it.
- `app-log(<what>)` — lines from the Tauri shell's tracing output (`make app-dev` redirected to a file).
- `sqlite-query(<SQL or what>)` — pasted `sqlite3` query and result against `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite`
  (or the scratch store named by `OBSERVATORY_CONFIG`).
- `file(<path>)` — the file (or the quoted excerpt) at the named path and commit.
- `git-log(<range or what>)` — pasted `git log` / `git diff` / `git worktree` output with the command.

## Tool vocabulary

`git`, `shell`, `make`, `cargo test`, `cli` (`observatory-cli replay|inspect|metrics`), `agent-browser`,
`tauri-smoke`, `sqlite3`, `gh`, `file` (report or document inspection).

## Surface rules (planning note 4)

- The browser host is the primary interactive surface: `trunk serve --config apps/observatory-app/ui/Trunk.toml
  --port 3141 --open false` from the active worktree, driven by `agent-browser --session <name>` (at most 3
  sessions per `trunk serve`, SPEC §5.8), the fixture opened through the file picker. Cold `trunk serve` is
  55.94 s, incremental 1.46–2.08 s.
- The Tauri window (`make app-dev`, 37.66 s to a running app) is a smoke check: the `observatory-app` process is
  alive, the dev log has the `Running .../debug/observatory-app` line with no `panicked` after it,
  `lsof -nP -iTCP:3141` lists `com.apple.WebKit` connections, System Events lists the app. Exactly one `trunk` owns
  3141 at a time: stop the standalone `trunk serve` before `make app-dev`; stop `cargo-tauri`, `trunk` and the app
  binary by PID afterwards. The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; what happens inside it is evidenced by the app
  log, the store, the CLI and the owner screenshot.
- At each milestone integration the owner takes one real screenshot with the display unlocked; its path is
  recorded in the boundary report and the session log (VAL-PROC-019).
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone; cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock (waits, not failures).
- Attach and host run only in the Tauri shell (the browser backend has no watcher, store or child process); the
  GitHub poll runs only in the Tauri shell. Scripted attach cases use `OBSERVATORY_CONFIG=<tmp>/config.toml` with
  `[ingest].factory_sessions_dir` pointing at a temp directory so `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written.
- Process assertions (worktree identity, red-before-green, `make check` in the worktree, coverage, commit rules,
  must-not-touch scope, Tauri smoke at m1–m5, fixture gitleaks) live once in the Process section with their
  milestone populations; area sections keep only milestone-specific gates.

## Area: S — Walking skeleton (milestone s)

Validator notes. Sources: planning notes 1, 3, 4, 5, 9, 11; architecture §1–6, §14–16; SPEC §3 "Common" and "S",
§6–8; `Makefile`; `.github/workflows/{mission-branch,release,bundle}.yml`; AGENTS.md; PRD §7. Fixed populations:
the nine lanes in PRD §7 order (`Intent`, `Orchestrator`, `Workers`, `Validators, scrutiny`, `Validators, user
testing`, `Integration`, `Human`, `Outside`, `Time, Waste, Cost and models`); the six S tests
(`replay_counts_every_line_of_a_capture`, `unknown_event_keeps_raw_type_and_byte_offset`,
`event_round_trips_through_serde`, `lanes_are_nine_in_prd_order`, `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file`,
`every_event_carries_the_mapping_version`); the S fixture `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` with
sidecar `.capture.json`. Process checks for `s` (worktree, red-before-green, `make check`, commit rules, coverage
reported, must-not-touch, gitleaks, `mission-checks` with the `machete` and `coverage` jobs) are in VAL-PROC-001
to VAL-PROC-010.

### VAL-SKEL-001: `make doctor` reports no missing required tool
In `<wt/s>`, `make doctor` exits 0 and its output contains an `ok` line for each of `rustup`, `cargo`, `cargo-deny`, `gitleaks`, `markdownlint-cli2`, `lychee`, `actionlint`, `jq` (section "required for 'make check':") and for `trunk` and `cargo-tauri` (section "required for the desktop app"). Any line beginning with `  missing` fails.

# Validation contract — mission `observatory-v1`

## Sources and precedence

This contract is synthesized from the seven area drafts in `contract-work/` (`skel.md`, `map.md`, `board.md`,
`host-control.md`, `gate.md`, `metrics.md`, `cross-process.md`). Where sources disagree the order is:
`planning-notes.md` (owner decisions after the spec, binding) > `SPEC.md` v0.2 > `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`
v0.6. `architecture.md` is the design reference: assertions whose only source is the architecture (file layouts,
log line names, config defaults not yet in `config/observatory.example.toml`, exact UI strings) are kept and
tagged `(source: architecture)` in their description; a worker who changes that design detail must change the
assertion through the orchestrator, not fail it silently. Numbers are the sources' numbers, pasted, never
estimated (RULES rule 7). Repository: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`; worktrees
`/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/<m>` on branch `wt/<m>` for `<m>` in `s`, `m0`,
`m1`, `m2`, `m3`, `m4`, `m5`; `<wt/m>` below means that worktree root.

## Evidence conventions

Each assertion ends with `Tool:` (one word from the vocabulary below) and `Evidence:` (a comma-separated list of
artifacts the validator attaches). Evidence items use these forms:

- `screenshot(<name>)` — a PNG taken by `agent-browser screenshot` (browser host) or, for the Tauri window, the
  owner's unlocked-display screenshot named `owner-screenshot(<path>)`.
- `snapshot(<name>)` — the text of `agent-browser snapshot` (accessibility tree) at that moment.
- `console-errors` — the output of `agent-browser console` and `agent-browser errors` (expected empty unless stated).
- `terminal-output(<command or what>)` — the pasted stdout/stderr and exit code of a shell command.
- `gh-output(<what>)` — pasted `gh` / `gh api` output with the command that produced it.
- `app-log(<what>)` — lines from the Tauri shell's tracing output (`make app-dev` redirected to a file).
- `sqlite-query(<SQL or what>)` — pasted `sqlite3` query and result against `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite`
  (or the scratch store named by `OBSERVATORY_CONFIG`).
- `file(<path>)` — the file (or the quoted excerpt) at the named path and commit.
- `git-log(<range or what>)` — pasted `git log` / `git diff` / `git worktree` output with the command.

## Tool vocabulary

`git`, `shell`, `make`, `cargo test`, `cli` (`observatory-cli replay|inspect|metrics`), `agent-browser`,
`tauri-smoke`, `sqlite3`, `gh`, `file` (report or document inspection).

## Surface rules (planning note 4)

- The browser host is the primary interactive surface: `trunk serve --config apps/observatory-app/ui/Trunk.toml
  --port 3141 --open false` from the active worktree, driven by `agent-browser --session <name>` (at most 3
  sessions per `trunk serve`, SPEC §5.8), the fixture opened through the file picker. Cold `trunk serve` is
  55.94 s, incremental 1.46–2.08 s.
- The Tauri window (`make app-dev`, 37.66 s to a running app) is a smoke check: the `observatory-app` process is
  alive, the dev log has the `Running .../debug/observatory-app` line with no `panicked` after it,
  `lsof -nP -iTCP:3141` lists `com.apple.WebKit` connections, System Events lists the app. Exactly one `trunk` owns
  3141 at a time: stop the standalone `trunk serve` before `make app-dev`; stop `cargo-tauri`, `trunk` and the app
  binary by PID afterwards. The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; what happens inside it is evidenced by the app
  log, the store, the CLI and the owner screenshot.
- At each milestone integration the owner takes one real screenshot with the display unlocked; its path is
  recorded in the boundary report and the session log (VAL-PROC-019).
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone; cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock (waits, not failures).
- Attach and host run only in the Tauri shell (the browser backend has no watcher, store or child process); the
  GitHub poll runs only in the Tauri shell. Scripted attach cases use `OBSERVATORY_CONFIG=<tmp>/config.toml` with
  `[ingest].factory_sessions_dir` pointing at a temp directory so `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written.
- Process assertions (worktree identity, red-before-green, `make check` in the worktree, coverage, commit rules,
  must-not-touch scope, Tauri smoke at m1–m5, fixture gitleaks) live once in the Process section with their
  milestone populations; area sections keep only milestone-specific gates.

## Area: S — Walking skeleton (milestone s)

Validator notes. Sources: planning notes 1, 3, 4, 5, 9, 11; architecture §1–6, §14–16; SPEC §3 "Common" and "S",
§6–8; `Makefile`; `.github/workflows/{mission-branch,release,bundle}.yml`; AGENTS.md; PRD §7. Fixed populations:
the nine lanes in PRD §7 order (`Intent`, `Orchestrator`, `Workers`, `Validators, scrutiny`, `Validators, user
testing`, `Integration`, `Human`, `Outside`, `Time, Waste, Cost and models`); the six S tests
(`replay_counts_every_line_of_a_capture`, `unknown_event_keeps_raw_type_and_byte_offset`,
`event_round_trips_through_serde`, `lanes_are_nine_in_prd_order`, `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file`,
`every_event_carries_the_mapping_version`); the S fixture `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` with
sidecar `.capture.json`. Process checks for `s` (worktree, red-before-green, `make check`, commit rules, coverage
reported, must-not-touch, gitleaks, `mission-checks` with the `machete` and `coverage` jobs) are in VAL-PROC-001
to VAL-PROC-010.

### VAL-SKEL-001: `make doctor` reports no missing required tool
In `<wt/s>`, `make doctor` exits 0 and its output contains an `ok` line for each of `rustup`, `cargo`, `cargo-deny`, `gitleaks`, `markdownlint-cli2`, `lychee`, `actionlint`, `jq` (section "required for 'make check':") and for `trunk` and `cargo-tauri` (section "required for the desktop app"). Any line beginning with `  missing` fails.
Tool: make
Evidence: terminal-output(make doctor, full)

### VAL-SKEL-002: Cargo workspace exists at the contract paths
At `<wt/s>` root `Cargo.toml` declares a workspace and `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 | jq -r '.packages[].name'` prints `observatory-core`, `observatory-cli`, `observatory-app` and `observatory-ui`; the manifests live at `crates/observatory-core/Cargo.toml`, `crates/observatory-cli/Cargo.toml`, `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` and `apps/observatory-app/ui/Cargo.toml` (architecture §2; `crates/observatory-core`, `crates/observatory-cli`, `apps/observatory-app` are the Makefile and CI probe contract per AGENTS.md). A missing package or a package at another path fails.
Tool: shell
Evidence: terminal-output(cargo metadata --no-deps | jq .packages[].name), terminal-output(ls of the four manifest paths)

### VAL-SKEL-003: `Cargo.lock` is committed
`git -C <wt/s> ls-files Cargo.lock` prints `Cargo.lock`, and `git check-ignore Cargo.lock` prints nothing (exit 1). An untracked or ignored lock file fails (SPEC §3 S outcome).
Tool: git
Evidence: terminal-output(git ls-files Cargo.lock), terminal-output(git check-ignore Cargo.lock; echo $?)

### VAL-SKEL-004: The six S tests exist and pass under `cargo test`
`cargo test --workspace --all-features` in `<wt/s>` exits 0 and its output contains one `test ... <name> ... ok` line for each of the six S tests named in the validator notes, and every `test result:` summary line reads `0 failed`. The tests carry the SPEC §3 S semantics: `event_round_trips_through_serde` serializes and deserializes one `Event` per `SourcePtr` variant (`Jsonl`, `Rpc`, `Git`, `GitHub`, `App`) and one with `EventKind::Unknown` (architecture §3; `rg -n 'SourcePtr::(Jsonl|Rpc|Git|GitHub|App)'` in the test file shows the five); `lanes_are_nine_in_prd_order` asserts `Lane::ALL: [Lane; 9]` ordered `Intent, Orchestrator, Workers, Scrutiny, UserTesting, Integration, Human, Outside, TimeWasteCost` with `name()` returning exactly the nine PRD strings and `number()` 1 to 9. A missing name, any `FAILED`, a round trip covering fewer than the five pointer variants, or a different lane count, order or name string fails.
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: terminal-output(cargo test --workspace --all-features, the six `ok` lines and every `test result:` line), terminal-output(rg SourcePtr variants in the serde test; rg 'ALL|fn name' crates/observatory-core/src/model/lane.rs)

### VAL-SKEL-005: CLI replay prints one line per event and ends with `unknown events: N`
In `<wt/s>`, `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` exits 0; its stdout's last line matches `^unknown events: [0-9]+$`; N > 0 is allowed (SPEC §3 S acceptance). The number of stdout lines before the summary equals the number of events, which in S equals the number of lines in the fixture (`wc -l < fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl`), because the S mapper yields exactly one `Unknown` event per raw line (SPEC §3 "every line is `unknown.event`, counted"; architecture §2 S row). A missing summary line, a summary line that is not last, or an event-line count different from the fixture line count fails.
Tool: cli
Evidence: terminal-output(replay stdout tail, `unknown events: N`), terminal-output(wc -l of the fixture), terminal-output(line count of replay stdout minus 1)

### VAL-SKEL-006: Every replayed S event is `Unknown`
On the S fixture, the `N` of `unknown events: N` printed by VAL-SKEL-005 equals the total event count (every event is `EventKind::Unknown`). `rg -n 'EventKind::' crates/observatory-core/src/mapping/` shows no constructor of a non-`Unknown` variant returned by `map_record` (the variants are declared in `model/kind.rs`; only `Unknown { raw_type }` is produced in S). N smaller than the event count, or a mapping rule producing a known kind, fails (SPEC §3 S "no mapping beyond `Unknown`").
Tool: cli
Evidence: terminal-output(unknown events: N vs event-line count), terminal-output(rg EventKind:: crates/observatory-core/src/mapping)

### VAL-SKEL-007: CLI exits non-zero on a missing file
`cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/does-not-exist.jsonl` exits with a non-zero code, prints an error naming the path on stderr and no `unknown events:` line on stdout, and `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file` in `crates/observatory-cli/tests/cli.rs` passes (`cargo test -p observatory-cli`). Exit 0 or a summary line on a missing path fails.
Tool: cli
Evidence: terminal-output(replay of a missing path with `echo $?`), terminal-output(cargo test -p observatory-cli summary line)

### VAL-SKEL-008: `make replay-fixtures` replays every `fixtures/streams/*.jsonl`
`make replay-fixtures` in `<wt/s>` exits 0 and prints `replay fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` (one `replay <path>` line per root `.jsonl` under `fixtures/streams/`, at S exactly that one); no `skipped` line. Non-zero exit or the `no fixtures/streams/*.jsonl yet, skipped` line fails.
Tool: make
Evidence: terminal-output(make replay-fixtures, full)

### VAL-SKEL-009: `Event` carries a `SourcePtr::Jsonl` pointer and `mapping_version`; `Unknown` keeps `raw_type` and the byte offset
`crates/observatory-core/src/model/event.rs` defines `pub struct Event` with fields `source: SourcePtr` and `mapping_version: MappingVersion`, and `pub enum SourcePtr` has a variant `Jsonl { path: PathBuf, byte_offset: u64, byte_len: u32 }` (architecture §3, invariant I4). `EventKind::Unknown { raw_type: String }` exists in `model/kind.rs`; for a raw line the mapper stores the line's `type` value (the five values planning note 1 lists: `message`, `session_start`, `todo_state`, `agent_turn_outcome`, `compaction_state`) in `raw_type`, `byte_offset` is the offset of the first byte of that line in the file and `byte_len` excludes the newline (architecture §4.2). `every_event_carries_the_mapping_version` and `unknown_event_keeps_raw_type_and_byte_offset` pass; a replayed S event serializes with `"mapping_version":"v1"` and `"source":"jsonl"`. The validator cross-checks one event of the S fixture: `head -c <byte_offset+byte_len> <fixture> | tail -c <byte_len>` is exactly the raw line (if the CLI prints offsets; otherwise the test is the evidence). With `[metrics].budget = 0.0` (default) and no launch `budget_usd`, the lane-9 panel shows no budget fraction and the meter is reported as disabled; with a budget greater than 0 (config key or launch `budget_usd`), the panel shows mission cost so far and the budget in the price table's currency and the fraction `cost_so_far / budget` (FR-M6; `[metrics].budget` default `(source: architecture §11)`). Pass: a core unit test covers both states and the browser host renders the disabled state for the fixture under the default config. Fail: a meter shown with budget 0, or a fraction that does not equal cost so far divided by the configured budget.

Evidence: terminal-output(unit test output for both states), snapshot(lane-9 panel under default config), terminal-output(cost-so-far and budget values from the test)

### VAL-METRIC-011: Model comparison reports cost and first-pass active time per completed feature by role and model
`MetricsReport` contains, for each role present in the fixture and for each model used in that role, `cost_per_completed_feature` and `first_pass_active_s_per_completed_feature`; for the fixture the three role models `claude-fable-5.1` (orchestrator), `claude-sonnet-5-5` (worker), `claude-opus-5-5` (scrutiny and user-testing validators) each appear with both figures, and each figure equals the role-model's total divided by its count of completed features (features with `task.done`, validation green and integrated, PRD §10.4 cycle definition) (FR-M7). Pass: the three rows are present in `--json` and in the lane-9 panel, and one row recomputes by hand from the per-feature values within 0.01 USD and 1 s. Fail: a role model missing, or a figure that does not recompute.
Tool: cli
Evidence: terminal-output(--json model-comparison section), terminal-output(hand recomputation of one row), snapshot(comparison table in the lane-9 panel)

### VAL-METRIC-012: Export to CSV and JSON from the UI in the browser host downloads the metrics rows
In `trunk serve --port 3141` with the fixture opened through the file picker, the lane-9 panel's export control offers CSV and JSON; choosing CSV triggers a browser download whose content equals the CLI `--csv` output for the same fixture (`diff` empty), and choosing JSON triggers a download that parses and equals the CLI `--json` rows (SPEC §3 M5 outcome "CSV/JSON export"). Pass: both downloads complete and both diffs are empty. Fail: no download, a download that differs from the CLI output, or a console error during export.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(export-control and the two clicks), terminal-output(downloaded file paths and diff outputs), console-errors

### VAL-METRIC-013: Export in the Tauri app writes a file on disk at the chosen path
In the Tauri app (`make app-dev`), the `export` command with `{ mission_id, format: Csv, path }` `(source: architecture §7)` writes an RFC 4180 CSV at `path` whose content equals the CLI `--csv` output for the same mission, returns `{ rows }` equal to the number of data rows, and the same holds for `format: Json` against `--json`. Pass: the file exists at the chosen path and `diff` against the CLI output is empty. Fail: no file, a different path, or a content difference. Under planning note 4 the export is performed by the owner at the M5 boundary (or by the validator if the dialog can be driven) and the validator checks the file on disk; the smoke set is VAL-PROC-005.
Tool: tauri-smoke
Evidence: terminal-output(ls -l <path>), terminal-output(diff output), file(who performed the export)

In the browser host with the fixture open, clicking Details on a milestone card and selecting the Cost and waste tab shows for that milestone: per-feature and per-role token counts (input, output, cache read, cache write) and cost with the price-table date `2026-10-22`, waste split by the eight causes, and the list of rework windows (open, close or unresolved, cause). The token totals shown equal the milestone row of the CLI `--csv` within 1 token and the cost within 0.01 USD. Pass: tab opens, all four sections present, totals agree. Fail: tab missing, a section empty while the CLI reports non-zero values, or totals disagree.
Tool: agent-browser
Evidence: snapshot(details-cost-and-waste), terminal-output(CLI milestone row and comparison of totals), screenshot(details-cost-and-waste)

### VAL-METRIC-015: Details tab "Review notes" (FR-D2) opens from a card and shows the fixture's findings
For the same card, the Review notes tab lists the scrutiny findings of the milestone with severity (blocking / non-blocking) and status (open / resolved) and the user-testing scenario results with their evidence references; the count of findings listed equals the count of `finding_blocking` plus `finding_non_blocking` events for that milestone in `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.events.json`, and the count of scenario results equals the count of `qa_scenario_passed` plus `qa_scenario_failed`. ### VAL-METRIC-016: Details tab "Validation criteria" (FR-D3) opens from a card and maps criteria to satisfying events
For the same card, the Validation criteria tab lists the acceptance criteria from the plan per feature of the milestone, and for each criterion either the event ids that satisfied it or an explicit unsatisfied marker; clicking a satisfying event id opens the scrubbed raw line (never the unscrubbed one). Pass: at least one feature of the fixture lists criteria, each criterion shows events or the unsatisfied marker, and the raw-line link works. ### VAL-METRIC-017: Details tab "Commits and integration" (FR-D4) opens from a card and shows the fixture's commits and integration events
For the same card, the Commits and integration tab lists the milestone's commits (from `commit_created` events), its worktree, integration into `mission/observatory-v1` (`integration_merged`), conflicts (`integration_conflict`, `integration_conflict_resolved`) and fast-check results (`gate_command_run`, `gate_command_passed`, `gate_command_failed`); the number of commits listed equals the count of `commit_created` events for that milestone in the golden events file and the wording uses "integrated in mission", never "merged", for lane-6 entries (PRD §7 lane 6 wording). ### VAL-METRIC-018: Details tab "Gate" (FR-D5) opens from a card and shows the gate state for the fixture
For the same card, the Gate tab shows the mission PR link, reviews, checks, attestations, merge policy with the rule that decided it, and merge history; for the M0 fixture, which has no PR into `main`, the tab shows the `Pending` gate state with empty reviews, checks and attestations sections and no error. The mission library (`list_missions` / `view::library` `(source: architecture §7)`) returns for each mission a `headline` with cycle seconds, waste seconds, token total and cost with the price-table date, and the library view in the browser host shows these next to name, date and event count for the fixture mission; the headline cost equals the sum of the fixture's milestone rows' `cost_usd` within 0.01 USD (SPEC §3 M1 outcome "headline metrics arrive with M5"). `reports/waste/m5.md` exists on `wt/m5` (and on `mission/observatory-v1` after integration), names the capture file and the exact CLI command it was produced from, and contains the pasted CLI output: waste seconds by the eight causes, the mission overhead line, rework window count by the four causes, tokens and cost with `price_table = 2026-10-22`. Re-running the named command on the same capture reproduces the numbers exactly (SPEC §8 `waste/<m>.md` "computed by the observatory on its own capture"; RULES rule 7). Pass: file present, command named, re-run matches. Fail: file absent, a number without a producing command, or a re-run that differs.

Evidence: git-log(git ls-files reports/waste/m5.md), terminal-output(the command line copied from the file), terminal-output(diff of the file's pasted block against the re-run output)

### VAL-METRIC-022: The frozen mapping and the M0 fixture are unchanged by M5
`shasum -a 256` of `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl`, `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.events.json`, `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.capture.json` and every file under `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.children/` on `wt/m5` and at the `m5` integration commit equals the hash of the same path at the M0 integration merge commit on `mission/observatory-v1` (the block recorded in the `m0` boundary report), and `git diff <m0-integration-sha>..wt/m5 --stat -- fixtures/streams/ crates/observatory-core/src/mapping/` is empty; `cargo test -p observatory-core --test mapping` stays green and `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl` still ends with `unknown events: 0` (SPEC §3 M5 "Must not touch: anything that changes the frozen mapping or the M0 fixture"; SPEC §5.2 "frozen at M0 and never edited"). Pass: all hashes equal, the diff is empty, both commands green. Fail: any hash differs, any path in the diff, or `unknown events` not 0.

## Area: M5 — Telemetry export (milestone m5)

Validator notes. Sources: SPEC §5.7, §5.9; PRD §11.4; D-004, D-010; architecture §10–§12;
`config/observatory.example.toml` `[telemetry]`; dependency readiness report "Grafana Cloud OTLP" (the keychain
string is `Authorization=Basic …`, 212 characters; sent whole the gateway answered 401, split on the first `=` it
answered 200 with body `{}`). The validator never prints, copies or deletes the keychain item
`droid-observatory/otlp-headers` (planning notes: keychain values are never printed; `security find-generic-password
-s <service>` only without `-w`). Status-bar strings and `TelemetryStatus.reason` values are `(source: architecture
§7, §10)`. The validator has no Grafana query credential in the sources; the Grafana screenshot is the owner's
(VAL-TELEM-008).

### VAL-TELEM-001: Worst-case exported series count is 182, under the budget of 200
`exported_series_count_is_under_budget_on_worst_case_labels()` is green: `SeriesPlan::from(&Config::default().telemetry).worst_case` equals 182, computed as 9 (`observatory.mission.cycle_seconds`, 6 buckets + `+Inf` + `_sum` + `_count`) + 8 (`observatory.feature.cycle_seconds`, 5 buckets + 3) + 64 (`observatory.waste_seconds`, 8 milestone labels × 8 causes) + 32 (`observatory.rework_windows`, 8 × 4) + 8 (`observatory.fix_loops`) + 48 (four `observatory.tokens.*` counters × 3 roles × 4 models) + 12 (`observatory.cost_usd`) + 1 (`observatory.unknown_events`), and 182 < `[telemetry].max_series` (200) (SPEC §5.7 table). Pass: the test asserts both the value 182 and the strict inequality and passes. Fail: a different count or a missing inequality.
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: terminal-output(cargo test -p observatory-core --test telemetry exported_series_count_is_under_budget_on_worst_case_labels), terminal-output(test body showing the per-metric terms)

### VAL-TELEM-002: Exporter refuses to start when the computed worst case is not under `max_series`
With a config whose `[telemetry].enabled = true` and `[telemetry].max_series = 182` (or any value at or below the computed worst case for the configured buckets and limits) the exporter does not start, `telemetry_status` reports `enabled = false` with a reason naming the computed count and the limit, and nothing is sent to the gateway; with `max_series = 200` and the same buckets the plan is accepted (SPEC §5.7 "the exporter refuses to start if its computed worst case ... is not under `[telemetry].max_series`"; test name and `TelemetryStatus` shape `(source: architecture §10)`). Pass: a unit test (suggested name `exporter_refuses_to_start_when_worst_case_reaches_max_series`) covers both values. Fail: an export attempt with `max_series` at or below the worst case, or a rejection at 200.
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: terminal-output(unit test output), terminal-output(TelemetryStatus.reason for the refused case)

### VAL-TELEM-003: Labels outside the allowed set are rejected
`labels_outside_allowed_set_are_rejected()` is green: `Label::parse` accepts exactly `mission`, `milestone`, `role`, `model`, `cause` (the `[telemetry].metric_labels_allowed` list, D-010) and returns `LabelError` for `session_id`, `event_id`, `feature`, `feature_id`, `status`, `class`, `unit`, `price_table` and any free-text name; none of the eleven exported instruments (VAL-TELEM-009) carries a label outside the five. Pass: the test asserts the five accepted names and at least the eight rejected names above. Fail: any name outside the five accepted, or any of the five rejected.

The `milestone` label value for the ninth and later distinct milestones of a mission (beyond `[telemetry].max_milestone_labels - 1 = 7` named values) is `overflow`, and the `model` label value for the fifth and later distinct models of a mission is `other`; the first seven milestones and the first four models keep their own values (SPEC §5.7 guards; SPEC §5.5 `max_milestone_labels` = 8; the `- 1` arithmetic `(source: architecture §10)`). With `Config::default()` (and with `config/observatory.example.toml` as the config file) `[telemetry].enabled` is `false` (D-004 works offline), `telemetry_status` returns `{ enabled: false, reason: "off in config" }`, the status bar reads `telemetry: off (config)`, and no connection to `otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net` is opened by the app process. `telemetry_stays_off_without_keychain_item_and_ui_says_so()` is green: with `[telemetry].enabled = true` and `secrets::otlp_headers()` returning `Ok(None)`, the exporter is not started, `telemetry_status` returns `{ enabled: false, reason: "no keychain item" }` and the status bar text is `telemetry: off, no keychain item <keychain_service>`, which under the default service is `telemetry: off, no keychain item droid-observatory/otlp-headers`. The live check uses a config whose `[telemetry].keychain_service` names a service that does not exist in the keychain (for example `droid-observatory/otlp-headers-absent`); the owner's real item is never deleted. The app does not read `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` from the environment (D-010: header value only from the keychain): setting it does not turn export on. `telemetry::parse_header("Authorization=Basic YWJj=")` returns `("Authorization", "Basic YWJj=")` (split on the first `=` only, the rest kept intact including later `=`), `parse_header("nodelimiter")` returns `None`, and the exporter sends the parsed name and value as one HTTP header (readiness report finding; function `(source: architecture §10)`). After an export cycle with the item present, the app log contains no line matching `Authorization=`, `Basic ` or the keychain value's first 8 characters, and `Secret`'s `Debug`/`Display` output is `<redacted>`; the `tracing` field filter drops fields named `authorization`, `token`, `header`, `secret` `(source: architecture §12)` (SPEC §5.9; invariant I7). ### VAL-TELEM-008: With the keychain item present and `enabled = true` the series appear in Grafana with only the allowed labels and resource attributes
With `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` present in the keychain (account `dct`, confirmed with `security find-generic-password -s droid-observatory/otlp-headers` without `-w`; planning note 2) and `[telemetry].enabled = true`, the status bar reads `telemetry: exporting since <timestamp>`, the app log records successful POSTs to `https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp/v1/metrics` every 15 s (status only, no header), and the owner's Grafana stack shows the mission's series with labels drawn only from `mission`, `milestone`, `role`, `model`, `cause` and resource attributes exactly `service.name=droid-observatory` and `service.version=<crate version>` (SPEC §3 M5 acceptance; SPEC §5.7 contract). ## 1. Assignment (from parent agent; authoritative, unchanged)

Mission dir `MD = /home/user/.factory/missions/e194b9e3-6a67-42b9-bfc9-dd4e1ac23b0c`. Do **not** modify the git repository `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory` (read-only; SPEC.md, ai/RULES.md, PRD may be read).

1. `MD/validation-contract.md` — header (title; one paragraph on sources/precedence: planning notes > SPEC v0.2 > PRD v0.6, architecture.md as design reference; evidence conventions screenshot, snapshot, console-errors, terminal-output(...), gh-output, app-log, sqlite-query, file, git-log; Tool vocabulary; surface rules from planning note 4). Then areas in this exact order with these exact headings: `## Area: S — Walking skeleton (milestone s)`, `## Area: M0 — Stream capture and mapping (milestone m0)`, `## Area: M1 — Board in replay and attach (milestone m1)`, `## Area: M2 — Host (milestone m2)`, `## Area: M3 — Intervention (milestone m3)`, `## Area: M4 — Mission branch, gate and fix loop (milestone m4)`, `## Area: M5 — Time, waste, cost (milestone m5)`, `## Area: M5 — Telemetry export (milestone m5)`, `## Cross-Area Flows`, `## Process and integration gates (milestone final)`. <coding_guidelines>
# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to the backlog (GitHub issues labelled `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`)
  as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs (rule 14).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to the backlog (GitHub issues labelled `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`)
  as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs (rule 14).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>



</system-reminder>
