## Area: M5 — Time, waste, cost (milestone m5)

Sources: SPEC.md §3 "Common" and "M5 — Time, waste, cost", §5.5–§5.7, §5.9, §6, §8; PRD v0.6 §7 lane 9, §10.1–10.5, FR-M1..M7, FR-D2..D6, FR-L4; architecture.md §9–§12; D-004, D-010; `config/observatory.example.toml`; `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`; `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`; planning notes (decisions 2 and 4 binding). Worktree for the milestone: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/m5` on branch `wt/m5`. Repository root below is `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`; the fixture is `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl`.

Closed lists used throughout (SPEC §5.6):

- Waste causes (8): `waiting_human_question`, `waiting_human_permission`, `waiting_merge`, `waiting_validation`, `rework`, `retry_failure`, `idle_queued`, `idle_unscheduled`.
- Rework causes (4): `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate`.
- Time states (6, PRD §10.1): Active, Waiting on human (sub-causes question, permission, merge), Waiting on validation, Retry and failure, Idle queued, Idle unscheduled.
- Details tabs added in M5 (5): Cost and waste (FR-D6), Review notes (FR-D2), Validation criteria (FR-D3), Commits and integration (FR-D4), Gate (FR-D5).
- Lane-9 chart types (3): stacked bars, timeline, sparkline.

Precondition (SPEC §3 M5 "Oracle", architecture §17): the owner's reference CSV must exist before any M5 metrics work starts. VAL-METRIC-001 states it; if it fails, the stall flag goes up and the remaining VAL-METRIC assertions are not evaluated until the owner supplies the file.

### VAL-METRIC-001: Reference CSV is present at the M4→M5 boundary
`reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv` is tracked on `mission/observatory-v1` at the M4→M5 boundary and its first line is exactly the 20-column header `scope,id,name,cycle_s,first_pass_active_s,rework_s,waste_waiting_human_question_s,waste_waiting_human_permission_s,waste_waiting_merge_s,waste_waiting_validation_s,waste_rework_s,waste_retry_failure_s,waste_idle_queued_s,waste_idle_unscheduled_s,rework_windows,tokens_input,tokens_output,tokens_cache_read,tokens_cache_write,cost_usd,price_table`. Pass: the file is tracked and the header matches byte for byte. Fail: file absent or header differs; the M5 integration feature raises the stall flag and asks the owner (SPEC §3 M5 "Missing at the M4→M5 boundary = stall flag, human input").
Tool: git
Evidence: `git -C /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory ls-files reports/reference/` output, first line of the CSV, boundary report line stating present or stall flag raised

### VAL-METRIC-002: CLI metrics --csv prints the column contract
`cargo run -p observatory-cli -- metrics fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl --csv` exits 0 and prints RFC 4180 CSV whose header equals the 20-column line in VAL-METRIC-001 and whose data rows have `scope` in {`feature`, `milestone`}, every `*_s` column an integer number of seconds, every `tokens_*` column an integer, `cost_usd` a decimal, and `price_table` equal to `2026-10-22`. Pass: header identical, no row violates any field rule. Fail: any extra, missing or reordered column, or any field outside its rule.
Tool: cli
Evidence: exit code, pasted header line, row count, pasted first feature row and first milestone row

### VAL-METRIC-003: Metrics match the owner's reference spreadsheet within tolerance (hard gate)
`cargo test -p observatory-core --test oracle` runs `metrics_match_reference_spreadsheet_within_tolerance()` green: for every row of `reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv` keyed by (`scope`, `id`) the engine produces a row where each duration column differs by at most 1 s, each token column by at most 1 token, `cost_usd` by at most 0.01 USD, `rework_windows` is equal, and `price_table` is equal; no reference row is missing from the engine output and no engine row is missing from the reference. Pass: test passes and the independent `diff` of the CLI `--csv` output against the reference shows only differences inside the tolerance. Fail: any row outside tolerance, any row missing on either side, or the test is skipped or ignored. This assertion is the milestone's hard gate (SPEC §3 M5 "Gate").
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: `cargo test -p observatory-core --test oracle` output with `test result: ok`, pasted per-column maximum deviations, `diff` of CLI CSV vs reference

### VAL-METRIC-004: CLI metrics --json prints a MetricsReport consistent with the CSV
`cargo run -p observatory-cli -- metrics fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl --json` exits 0 and prints one JSON document (`MetricsReport`) that parses, and for each feature and milestone row of the `--csv` output the same (`scope`, `id`) entry exists in the JSON with equal `cycle_s`, `first_pass_active_s`, `rework_s`, `rework_windows`, token counts and `cost_usd`, and a `price_table` field equal to `2026-10-22`. Pass: JSON parses and every CSV row has an equal JSON counterpart. Fail: parse error or any disagreement between the two outputs.
Tool: cli
Evidence: exit code, `jq` parse success, comparison script output listing rows compared and rows disagreeing (must be 0)

### VAL-METRIC-005: Time states partition every instant exactly once
`time_states_partition_every_instant_exactly_once()` is green: for each feature of the fixture, `metrics::partition(events_of_feature, end)` returns intervals that are contiguous (each `to` equals the next `from`), non-overlapping, start at the feature's first event and end at `end`, and each interval carries exactly one of the six states Active, WaitingHuman(Question|Permission|Merge), WaitingValidation, RetryFailure, IdleQueued, IdleUnscheduled, so the sum of interval lengths equals the elapsed time of the feature. Pass: test passes against the fixture's features. Fail: a gap, an overlap, or a feature whose intervals do not sum to its elapsed time.
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: `cargo test -p observatory-core time_states_partition_every_instant_exactly_once` output, test body asserting contiguity and the sum equality

### VAL-METRIC-006: A rework window closes on its resolution event
`rework_window_closes_on_resolution()` is green for each of the four PRD §10.2 pairs: `finding.blocking` closes on `rework.resolved`; `qa.scenario.failed` closes on `qa.scenario.passed` for the same scenario (a pass for a different scenario does not close it); `integration.conflict` closes on `integration.conflict_resolved`; `check.failed` closes on `check.passed` for the same check (a pass for a different check does not close it). Each window carries exactly one rework cause from {`scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate`} matching its opening kind (lane 4 → `scrutiny`, lane 5 → `user_testing`, lane 6 → `integration`, lane 8 → `gate`). Pass: all four pairs close and the mismatched-scenario and mismatched-check cases stay open. Fail: any pair does not close, closes on the wrong event, or carries a different cause.
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: `cargo test -p observatory-core rework_window_closes_on_resolution` output, test body showing the four pairs and the two same-key negative cases

### VAL-METRIC-007: Overlapping rework windows on one feature merge into one
`overlapping_windows_merge_on_one_feature()` is green: two windows on the same feature whose intervals overlap in time are reported as one window spanning the earliest open to the latest close, with `rework_windows` counting 1 for that span; two windows on different features that overlap in time are not merged (count 2). Pass: both cases hold. Fail: overlapping windows on one feature counted twice, or windows across features merged.
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: `cargo test -p observatory-core overlapping_windows_merge_on_one_feature` output

### VAL-METRIC-008: An unresolved window is reported at mission end
`unresolved_window_is_reported_at_mission_end()` is green: a window opened by a blocking signal with no closing event is kept open until the mission's last event, reported with `closed_by = None` (shown as unresolved), and its active time is counted as rework time up to mission end. Pass: the window appears in the report as unresolved and contributes to `rework_s`. Fail: the window is dropped, silently closed, or excluded from `rework_s`.
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: `cargo test -p observatory-core unresolved_window_is_reported_at_mission_end` output, Details Cost and waste tab listing the unresolved window for a fixture feature if the fixture has one (pasted count)

### VAL-METRIC-009: First-pass active time excludes rework windows
`first_pass_excludes_rework_windows()` is green: for a feature with Active intervals both inside and outside a rework window, `first_pass_active_s` equals the Active time outside every rework window, `rework_s` equals the Active time inside the windows, and `first_pass_active_s + rework_s` equals the feature's total Active time. Pass: the three equalities hold. Fail: any Active time inside a window counted as first pass, or the sum differs from total Active time.
Tool: cargo test

1→# Validation contract — mission `observatory-v1`
2→
3→## Sources and precedence
4→
5→This contract is synthesized from the seven area drafts in `contract-work/` (`skel.md`, `map.md`, `board.md`,
6→`host-control.md`, `gate.md`, `metrics.md`, `cross-process.md`). Where sources disagree the order is:
7→`planning-notes.md` (owner decisions after the spec, binding) > `SPEC.md` v0.2 > `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`
8→v0.6. `architecture.md` is the design reference: assertions whose only source is the architecture (file layouts,
9→log line names, config defaults not yet in `config/observatory.example.toml`, exact UI strings) are kept and
10→tagged `(source: architecture)` in their description; a worker who changes that design detail must change the
11→assertion through the orchestrator, not fail it silently. Numbers are the sources' numbers, pasted, never
12→estimated (RULES rule 7). Repository: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`; worktrees
13→`/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/<m>` on branch `wt/<m>` for `<m>` in `s`, `m0`,
14→`m1`, `m2`, `m3`, `m4`, `m5`; `<wt/m>` below means that worktree root.
15→
16→## Evidence conventions
17→
18→Each assertion ends with `Tool:` (one word from the vocabulary below) and `Evidence:` (a comma-separated list of
19→artifacts the validator attaches). Evidence items use these forms:
20→
21→- `screenshot(<name>)` — a PNG taken by `agent-browser screenshot` (browser host) or, for the Tauri window, the
22→  owner's unlocked-display screenshot named `owner-screenshot(<path>)`.
23→- `snapshot(<name>)` — the text of `agent-browser snapshot` (accessibility tree) at that moment.
24→- `console-errors` — the output of `agent-browser console` and `agent-browser errors` (expected empty unless stated).
25→- `terminal-output(<command or what>)` — the pasted stdout/stderr and exit code of a shell command.
26→- `gh-output(<what>)` — pasted `gh` / `gh api` output with the command that produced it.
27→- `app-log(<what>)` — lines from the Tauri shell's tracing output (`make app-dev` redirected to a file).
28→- `sqlite-query(<SQL or what>)` — pasted `sqlite3` query and result against `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite`
29→  (or the scratch store named by `OBSERVATORY_CONFIG`).
30→- `file(<path>)` — the file (or the quoted excerpt) at the named path and commit.
31→- `git-log(<range or what>)` — pasted `git log` / `git diff` / `git worktree` output with the command.
32→
33→## Tool vocabulary
34→
35→`git`, `shell`, `make`, `cargo test`, `cli` (`observatory-cli replay|inspect|metrics`), `agent-browser`,
36→`tauri-smoke`, `sqlite3`, `gh`, `file` (report or document inspection).
37→
38→## Surface rules (planning note 4)
39→
40→- The browser host is the primary interactive surface: `trunk serve --config apps/observatory-app/ui/Trunk.toml
41→  --port 3141 --open false` from the active worktree, driven by `agent-browser --session <name>` (at most 3
42→  sessions per `trunk serve`, SPEC §5.8), the fixture opened through the file picker. Cold `trunk serve` is
43→  55.94 s, incremental 1.46–2.08 s.
44→- The Tauri window (`make app-dev`, 37.66 s to a running app) is a smoke check: the `observatory-app` process is
45→  alive, the dev log has the `Running .../debug/observatory-app` line with no `panicked` after it,
46→  `lsof -nP -iTCP:3141` lists `com.apple.WebKit` connections, System Events lists the app. Exactly one `trunk` owns
47→  3141 at a time: stop the standalone `trunk serve` before `make app-dev`; stop `cargo-tauri`, `trunk` and the app
48→  binary by PID afterwards. The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; what happens inside it is evidenced by the app
49→  log, the store, the CLI and the owner screenshot.
50→- At each milestone integration the owner takes one real screenshot with the display unlocked; its path is
51→  recorded in the boundary report and the session log (VAL-PROC-019).
52→- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone; cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock (waits, not failures).
53→- Attach and host run only in the Tauri shell (the browser backend has no watcher, store or child process); the
54→  GitHub poll runs only in the Tauri shell. Scripted attach cases use `OBSERVATORY_CONFIG=<tmp>/config.toml` with
55→  `[ingest].factory_sessions_dir` pointing at a temp directory so `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written.
56→- Process assertions (worktree identity, red-before-green, `make check` in the worktree, coverage, commit rules,
57→  must-not-touch scope, Tauri smoke at m1–m5, fixture gitleaks) live once in the Process section with their
58→  milestone populations; area sections keep only milestone-specific gates.
59→
60→## Area: S — Walking skeleton (milestone s)
61→
62→Validator notes. Sources: planning notes 1, 3, 4, 5, 9, 11; architecture §1–6, §14–16; SPEC §3 "Common" and "S",
63→§6–8; `Makefile`; `.github/workflows/{mission-branch,release,bundle}.yml`; AGENTS.md; PRD §7. Fixed populations:
64→the nine lanes in PRD §7 order (`Intent`, `Orchestrator`, `Workers`, `Validators, scrutiny`, `Validators, user
65→testing`, `Integration`, `Human`, `Outside`, `Time, Waste, Cost and models`); the six S tests
66→(`replay_counts_every_line_of_a_capture`, `unknown_event_keeps_raw_type_and_byte_offset`,
67→`event_round_trips_through_serde`, `lanes_are_nine_in_prd_order`, `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file`,
68→`every_event_carries_the_mapping_version`); the S fixture `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` with
69→sidecar `.capture.json`. Process checks for `s` (worktree, red-before-green, `make check`, commit rules, coverage
70→reported, must-not-touch, gitleaks, `mission-checks` with the `machete` and `coverage` jobs) are in VAL-PROC-001
71→to VAL-PROC-010.
72→
73→### VAL-SKEL-001: `make doctor` reports no missing required tool
74→In `<wt/s>`, `make doctor` exits 0 and its output contains an `ok` line for each of `rustup`, `cargo`, `cargo-deny`, `gitleaks`, `markdownlint-cli2`, `lychee`, `actionlint`, `jq` (section "required for 'make check':") and for `trunk` and `cargo-tauri` (section "required for the desktop app"). Any line beginning with `  missing` fails.

## ### VAL-SKEL-001: Worktree is `../observatory-wt/s` on branch `wt/s`
`git -C /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/s rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` prints exactly `wt/s`, and `git -C /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory worktree list --porcelain` contains a `worktree /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/s` block whose `branch` line is `refs/heads/wt/s`. Any other path or branch fails.
## ### VAL-SKEL-002: `wt/s` touches no shared or off-limits file
`git -C <worktree> diff --name-only mission/observatory-v1...wt/s` lists none of `SPEC.md`, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `docs/decisions/README.md`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, and `git -C <repo> log origin/main..main` is empty (nothing was written to `main`). Fail if any of the five paths appears or `main` moved.
## ### VAL-SKEL-003: Red test commit precedes the green commit for each of the six S tests
For each of the six S tests, `git -C <worktree> log --reverse --format=%h -S'<test_name>' mission/observatory-v1..wt/s` yields a first commit C_red that introduces the test function; checking out C_red in a scratch worktree (`git worktree add /tmp/skel-red-<n> <C_red>`) and running `cargo test --workspace --all-features <test_name>` there exits non-zero (compile error or `test result: FAILED`); and a later commit on `wt/s` (first-parent order) makes the same command exit 0. The scrutiny validator also confirms the red run appears in the worker's session log (planning notes: "the scrutiny validator checks the red run exists in the worker log"). A test whose first commit already passes, or whose only commit also contains the implementation that makes it pass, fails this assertion for that test name.
## ### VAL-SKEL-004: Commits on `wt/s` follow the subject and trailer rules
`git -C <worktree> log --format='%h %s' mission/observatory-v1..wt/s` shows every subject at 72 characters or fewer, and `git log --format='%h%n%b' mission/observatory-v1..wt/s` shows the trailer `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` on every agent commit. `git reflog show wt/s` contains no `reset`, `rebase`, `amend` or `commit (amend)` entry (forward only, rule 12). Any violation fails.
## ### VAL-SKEL-008: `make check` exits 0 in the worktree
In `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/s`, `make check` (check-docs, check-links, check-workflows, check-file-size, check-todos, check-decisions-index, check-secrets, fmt-check, lint, test, deny, replay-fixtures, plus `machete` per architecture §15) exits 0 with no `skipped` line for `fmt-check`, `lint`, `test`, `deny` or `replay-fixtures` (those `skipped` lines mean `Cargo.toml` or the fixture was not found). Non-zero exit or any Rust target reporting `no Cargo.toml yet, skipped` fails.
## ### VAL-SKEL-023: The fixture directory passes `gitleaks detect --no-git`
`gitleaks detect --no-git --no-banner --redact --source fixtures/streams` exits 0 and reports no leaks (`no leaks found`), and the `.capture.json` `gitleaks` field records the clean run with its date (architecture §4.2 header example `"gitleaks": "clean 2026-10-22"`). Also `make check-secrets` (gitleaks over the git history) exits 0 as part of VAL-SKEL-008. Any finding fails and blocks the fixture.
## ### VAL-SKEL-027: Coverage of `observatory-core` is measured and pasted
Running alone (no other cargo build or validator session active, planning note 5), `make coverage` or `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --all-features --fail-under-lines 0 --summary-only` exits 0 in the worktree and prints the `TOTAL` summary line; the validator pastes that line verbatim (lines covered and percentage) into the report (rule 7: pasted, never estimated). No line is a pass/fail threshold in S; a missing summary line, a non-zero exit, or an estimated number fails.
## ### VAL-SKEL-031: `mission-checks` is green on the integration push of `wt/s`
Observed at S integration (the workflow triggers on `mission/**`, not on `wt/s`): after `git merge --no-ff wt/s` into `mission/observatory-v1` is pushed, `gh api '/repos/dctellya/droid-observatory/actions/runs?branch=mission/observatory-v1&head_sha=<merge sha>' --jq '.workflow_runs[] | select(.name=="mission-branch") | .conclusion'` prints `success`, and the run's job list (`gh run view <id> --json jobs --jq '.jobs[] | "\(.name) \(.conclusion)"'`) shows `machete success` and `coverage success` among the jobs (planning note 6: read via Actions runs, never the check-runs API). A `failure` conclusion, or a run without the `machete` and `coverage` jobs, fails.
## ### VAL-MAP-004: Fixture directory is gitleaks-clean
`gitleaks detect --no-git --no-banner -s <repo>/fixtures/streams` exits 0 with `no leaks found` (SPEC §3 common: a fixture is committed only after this scan is clean and a reviewer read it). Also `make check-secrets` (`gitleaks git --no-banner --redact .`) exits 0 in the worktree. Fail on exit code 1 or any reported finding.
## ### VAL-MAP-027: M0 touches nothing beyond its scope (no UI, no git/GitHub adapters, no metrics)
In `<repo>`: the directories `crates/observatory-core/src/view`, `crates/observatory-core/src/metrics`, `crates/observatory-core/src/control` and the files `crates/observatory-core/src/ingest/{watch,rpc,git,github,forge}.rs` do not exist; `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 | jq '.packages[] | select(.name=="observatory-core") | .dependencies[].name'` lists neither `ureq`, `notify`, nor `tokio`; `git diff --name-only $(git merge-base wt/m0 mission/observatory-v1) wt/m0 -- apps/observatory-app/ui/src` lists no new component directories (`board/`, `details/`, `agents/`, `lane9/`, `launch/` absent), so the window still shows the nine empty named lanes from S. Fail if any listed module, dependency or UI directory is present.
## ### VAL-MAP-028: Red tests are committed before the code that turns them green in `wt/m0`
`git log --reverse --format='%h %s' $(git merge-base wt/m0 mission/observatory-v1)..wt/m0 -- crates/observatory-core/tests/mapping.rs crates/observatory-core/tests/store.rs crates/observatory-cli/tests/cli.rs` shows, for each of the seven M0 tests named in SPEC §3, a commit adding the test that precedes (in `--reverse` order) the first commit under `crates/observatory-core/src/mapping/v1/`, `crates/observatory-core/src/store/` or `crates/observatory-cli/src/inspect.rs` that makes it pass; the worker's tool-call log under `build-log/<date>/*.jsonl` contains a `cargo test` call whose output has `test result: FAILED` for that test before the green run (rule 1; SPEC §3 common). Every commit on the range carries the trailer `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`, and `git reflog`/`git log` show no amend, reset or force-push (rule 12). Fail if any test first appears in the same commit as, or after, its implementation, or if no red run is logged.
## ### VAL-MAP-029: `make check` exits 0 in the M0 worktree
`make check` in `<repo>` (network available for `check-links`) exits 0, running `check-docs check-links check-workflows check-file-size check-todos check-decisions-index check-secrets fmt-check lint test deny replay-fixtures` in that order; `lint` is `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`. Paste the exit code and the `test result:` lines of `make test`. Fail on any non-zero sub-target.
## ### VAL-MAP-030: Fixture files are exempt from the 200 KB limit and every other tracked file is under it
`make check-file-size` (`MAX_FILE_KB=200`, `scripts/check-file-size.sh`) exits 0 in `<repo>`. `git ls-files | grep -v -E '^(fixtures/streams/|build-log/|Cargo.lock$)' | grep -v -E '\.(png|webp|mp4)$' | xargs wc -c | sort -n | tail -3` shows every listed file at or under 204800 bytes, including `docs/decisions/D-0NN-mapping-v1.md` and `crates/observatory-core/src/mapping/v1/kinds.rs`. Files under `fixtures/streams/` (the `.jsonl`, `.children/*.jsonl`, `.settings.json`, `.events.json`, `.capture.json`) may exceed 200 KB; record their sizes with `wc -c`. Fail if `check-file-size` exits non-zero or any non-exempt file is over 204800 bytes.
## ### VAL-BOARD-037: Tauri smoke check passes
Stop any standalone `trunk serve` on 3141, run `make app-dev` from `wt/m1` with the log redirected to a file. Within 120 s the log contains `Running .../debug/observatory-app` with no `panicked` line after it; `ps -p <pid>` shows the app binary alive 30 s later; `lsof -nP -iTCP:3141` lists at least one `com.apple.WebKit` ESTABLISHED connection; `osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to get name of every process whose background only is false'` includes the app process. The M1 integration report names the path of one screenshot taken by the owner with the display unlocked, showing the Tauri window with the board (planning note 4). On `git diff <m0-integration-sha>..wt/m1 --stat` and the source tree of `wt/m1`: no `host.rs`, `rpc.rs`, `github.rs`, `forge.rs` or `control/` module contains implementation (absent or empty stubs declared in S are allowed); the Tauri command table has none of `host_launch`, `host_control`, `human_action`, `gate`, `merge`; `ureq` is not a dependency of any crate in `Cargo.lock` diff for M1; while the app runs (VAL-BOARD-037) `lsof -nP -a -p <app pid> -iTCP` shows only connections to `127.0.0.1:3141` or `[::1]:3141`. # Validation contract — mission `observatory-v1`

## Sources and precedence

This contract is synthesized from the seven area drafts in `contract-work/` (`skel.md`, `map.md`, `board.md`,
`host-control.md`, `gate.md`, `metrics.md`, `cross-process.md`). Where sources disagree the order is:
`planning-notes.md` (owner decisions after the spec, binding) > `SPEC.md` v0.2 > `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`
v0.6. `architecture.md` is the design reference: assertions whose only source is the architecture (file layouts,
log line names, config defaults not yet in `config/observatory.example.toml`, exact UI strings) are kept and
tagged `(source: architecture)` in their description; a worker who changes that design detail must change the
assertion through the orchestrator, not fail it silently. Numbers are the sources' numbers, pasted, never
estimated (RULES rule 7). Repository: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`; worktrees
`/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/<m>` on branch `wt/<m>` for `<m>` in `s`, `m0`,
`m1`, `m2`, `m3`, `m4`, `m5`; `<wt/m>` below means that worktree root.

## Evidence conventions

Each assertion ends with `Tool:` (one word from the vocabulary below) and `Evidence:` (a comma-separated list of
artifacts the validator attaches). Evidence items use these forms:

- `screenshot(<name>)` — a PNG taken by `agent-browser screenshot` (browser host) or, for the Tauri window, the
  owner's unlocked-display screenshot named `owner-screenshot(<path>)`.
- `snapshot(<name>)` — the text of `agent-browser snapshot` (accessibility tree) at that moment.
- `console-errors` — the output of `agent-browser console` and `agent-browser errors` (expected empty unless stated).
- `terminal-output(<command or what>)` — the pasted stdout/stderr and exit code of a shell command.
- `gh-output(<what>)` — pasted `gh` / `gh api` output with the command that produced it.
- `app-log(<what>)` — lines from the Tauri shell's tracing output (`make app-dev` redirected to a file).
- `sqlite-query(<SQL or what>)` — pasted `sqlite3` query and result against `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite`
  (or the scratch store named by `OBSERVATORY_CONFIG`).
- `file(<path>)` — the file (or the quoted excerpt) at the named path and commit.
- `git-log(<range or what>)` — pasted `git log` / `git diff` / `git worktree` output with the command.

## Tool vocabulary

`git`, `shell`, `make`, `cargo test`, `cli` (`observatory-cli replay|inspect|metrics`), `agent-browser`,
`tauri-smoke`, `sqlite3`, `gh`, `file` (report or document inspection).

## Surface rules (planning note 4)

- The browser host is the primary interactive surface: `trunk serve --config apps/observatory-app/ui/Trunk.toml
  --port 3141 --open false` from the active worktree, driven by `agent-browser --session <name>` (at most 3
  sessions per `trunk serve`, SPEC §5.8), the fixture opened through the file picker. Cold `trunk serve` is
  55.94 s, incremental 1.46–2.08 s.
- The Tauri window (`make app-dev`, 37.66 s to a running app) is a smoke check: the `observatory-app` process is
  alive, the dev log has the `Running .../debug/observatory-app` line with no `panicked` after it,
  `lsof -nP -iTCP:3141` lists `com.apple.WebKit` connections, System Events lists the app. Exactly one `trunk` owns
  3141 at a time: stop the standalone `trunk serve` before `make app-dev`; stop `cargo-tauri`, `trunk` and the app
  binary by PID afterwards. The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; what happens inside it is evidenced by the app
  log, the store, the CLI and the owner screenshot.
- At each milestone integration the owner takes one real screenshot with the display unlocked; its path is
  recorded in the boundary report and the session log (VAL-PROC-019).
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone; cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock (waits, not failures).
- Attach and host run only in the Tauri shell (the browser backend has no watcher, store or child process); the
  GitHub poll runs only in the Tauri shell. Scripted attach cases use `OBSERVATORY_CONFIG=<tmp>/config.toml` with
  `[ingest].factory_sessions_dir` pointing at a temp directory so `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written.
- Process assertions (worktree identity, red-before-green, `make check` in the worktree, coverage, commit rules,
  must-not-touch scope, Tauri smoke at m1–m5, fixture gitleaks) live once in the Process section with their
  milestone populations; area sections keep only milestone-specific gates.

## Area: S — Walking skeleton (milestone s)

Validator notes. Sources: planning notes 1, 3, 4, 5, 9, 11; architecture §1–6, §14–16; SPEC §3 "Common" and "S",
§6–8; `Makefile`; `.github/workflows/{mission-branch,release,bundle}.yml`; AGENTS.md; PRD §7. Fixed populations:
the nine lanes in PRD §7 order (`Intent`, `Orchestrator`, `Workers`, `Validators, scrutiny`, `Validators, user
testing`, `Integration`, `Human`, `Outside`, `Time, Waste, Cost and models`); the six S tests
(`replay_counts_every_line_of_a_capture`, `unknown_event_keeps_raw_type_and_byte_offset`,
`event_round_trips_through_serde`, `lanes_are_nine_in_prd_order`, `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file`,
`every_event_carries_the_mapping_version`); the S fixture `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` with
sidecar `.capture.json`. Process checks for `s` (worktree, red-before-green, `make check`, commit rules, coverage
reported, must-not-touch, gitleaks, `mission-checks` with the `machete` and `coverage` jobs) are in VAL-PROC-001
to VAL-PROC-010.

### VAL-SKEL-001: `make doctor` reports no missing required tool
In `<wt/s>`, `make doctor` exits 0 and its output contains an `ok` line for each of `rustup`, `cargo`, `cargo-deny`, `gitleaks`, `markdownlint-cli2`, `lychee`, `actionlint`, `jq` (section "required for 'make check':") and for `trunk` and `cargo-tauri` (section "required for the desktop app"). Any line beginning with `  missing` fails.
Tool: make
Evidence: terminal-output(make doctor, full)

### VAL-SKEL-002: Cargo workspace exists at the contract paths
At `<wt/s>` root `Cargo.toml` declares a workspace and `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 | jq -r '.packages[].name'` prints `observatory-core`, `observatory-cli`, `observatory-app` and `observatory-ui`; the manifests live at `crates/observatory-core/Cargo.toml`, `crates/observatory-cli/Cargo.toml`, `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` and `apps/observatory-app/ui/Cargo.toml` (architecture §2; `crates/observatory-core`, `crates/observatory-cli`, `apps/observatory-app` are the Makefile and CI probe contract per AGENTS.md). A missing package or a package at another path fails.
Tool: shell
Evidence: terminal-output(cargo metadata --no-deps | jq .packages[].name), terminal-output(ls of the four manifest paths)

### VAL-SKEL-003: `Cargo.lock` is committed
`git -C <wt/s> ls-files Cargo.lock` prints `Cargo.lock`, and `git check-ignore Cargo.lock` prints nothing (exit 1). An untracked or ignored lock file fails (SPEC §3 S outcome).
Tool: git
Evidence: terminal-output(git ls-files Cargo.lock), terminal-output(git check-ignore Cargo.lock; echo $?)

### VAL-SKEL-004: The six S tests exist and pass under `cargo test`
`cargo test --workspace --all-features` in `<wt/s>` exits 0 and its output contains one `test ... <name> ... ok` line for each of the six S tests named in the validator notes, and every `test result:` summary line reads `0 failed`. The tests carry the SPEC §3 S semantics: `event_round_trips_through_serde` serializes and deserializes one `Event` per `SourcePtr` variant (`Jsonl`, `Rpc`, `Git`, `GitHub`, `App`) and one with `EventKind::Unknown` (architecture §3; `rg -n 'SourcePtr::(Jsonl|Rpc|Git|GitHub|App)'` in the test file shows the five); `lanes_are_nine_in_prd_order` asserts `Lane::ALL: [Lane; 9]` ordered `Intent, Orchestrator, Workers, Scrutiny, UserTesting, Integration, Human, Outside, TimeWasteCost` with `name()` returning exactly the nine PRD strings and `number()` 1 to 9. A missing name, any `FAILED`, a round trip covering fewer than the five pointer variants, or a different lane count, order or name string fails.
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: terminal-output(cargo test --workspace --all-features, the six `ok` lines and every `test result:` line), terminal-output(rg SourcePtr variants in the serde test; rg 'ALL|fn name' crates/observatory-core/src/model/lane.rs)

### VAL-SKEL-005: CLI replay prints one line per event and ends with `unknown events: N`
In `<wt/s>`, `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` exits 0; its stdout's last line matches `^unknown events: [0-9]+$`; N > 0 is allowed (SPEC §3 S acceptance). The number of stdout lines before the summary equals the number of events, which in S equals the number of lines in the fixture (`wc -l < fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl`), because the S mapper yields exactly one `Unknown` event per raw line (SPEC §3 "every line is `unknown.event`, counted"; architecture §2 S row). A missing summary line, a summary line that is not last, or an event-line count different from the fixture line count fails.
Tool: cli
Evidence: terminal-output(replay stdout tail, `unknown events: N`), terminal-output(wc -l of the fixture), terminal-output(line count of replay stdout minus 1)

### VAL-SKEL-006: Every replayed S event is `Unknown`
On the S fixture, the `N` of `unknown events: N` printed by VAL-SKEL-005 equals the total event count (every event is `EventKind::Unknown`). `rg -n 'EventKind::' crates/observatory-core/src/mapping/` shows no constructor of a non-`Unknown` variant returned by `map_record` (the variants are declared in `model/kind.rs`; only `Unknown { raw_type }` is produced in S). N smaller than the event count, or a mapping rule producing a known kind, fails (SPEC §3 S "no mapping beyond `Unknown`").
Tool: cli
Evidence: terminal-output(unknown events: N vs event-line count), terminal-output(rg EventKind:: crates/observatory-core/src/mapping)

### VAL-SKEL-007: CLI exits non-zero on a missing file
`cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/does-not-exist.jsonl` exits with a non-zero code, prints an error naming the path on stderr and no `unknown events:` line on stdout, and `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file` in `crates/observatory-cli/tests/cli.rs` passes (`cargo test -p observatory-cli`). Exit 0 or a summary line on a missing path fails.
Tool: cli
Evidence: terminal-output(replay of a missing path with `echo $?`), terminal-output(cargo test -p observatory-cli summary line)

### VAL-SKEL-008: `make replay-fixtures` replays every `fixtures/streams/*.jsonl`
`make replay-fixtures` in `<wt/s>` exits 0 and prints `replay fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` (one `replay <path>` line per root `.jsonl` under `fixtures/streams/`, at S exactly that one); no `skipped` line. Non-zero exit or the `no fixtures/streams/*.jsonl yet, skipped` line fails.
Tool: make
Evidence: terminal-output(make replay-fixtures, full)

### VAL-SKEL-009: `Event` carries a `SourcePtr::Jsonl` pointer and `mapping_version`; `Unknown` keeps `raw_type` and the byte offset
`crates/observatory-core/src/model/event.rs` defines `pub struct Event` with fields `source: SourcePtr` and `mapping_version: MappingVersion`, and `pub enum SourcePtr` has a variant `Jsonl { path: PathBuf, byte_offset: u64, byte_len: u32 }` (architecture §3, invariant I4). `EventKind::Unknown { raw_type: String }` exists in `model/kind.rs`; for a raw line the mapper stores the line's `type` value (the five values planning note 1 lists: `message`, `session_start`, `todo_state`, `agent_turn_outcome`, `compaction_state`) in `raw_type`, `byte_offset` is the offset of the first byte of that line in the file and `byte_len` excludes the newline (architecture §4.2). `every_event_carries_the_mapping_version` and `unknown_event_keeps_raw_type_and_byte_offset` pass; a replayed S event serializes with `"mapping_version":"v1"` and `"source":"jsonl"`. The validator cross-checks one event of the S fixture: `head -c <byte_offset+byte_len> <fixture> | tail -c <byte_len>` is exactly the raw line (if the CLI prints offsets; otherwise the test is the evidence). A struct without either field, a `Jsonl` pointer without `byte_offset`, a placeholder `raw_type`, or an offset counted in lines fails.
Tool: cargo test
Evidence: terminal-output(rg -n 'mapping_version|SourcePtr|Jsonl' crates/observatory-core/src/model/event.rs), terminal-output(cargo test every_event_carries_the_mapping_version unknown_event_keeps_raw_type_and_byte_offset), terminal-output(head -c / tail -c slice vs one fixture line, when offsets are printed)
